text: Gravity's MacDowell-Mansouri action needs a fixed-norm internal vector whose covariant derivative is the tetrad, and the framework supplies it from the frozen point, the parallel scale tractor of the geometry paper whose squared norm is the cosmological constant. The frozen point is parallel, so it is not the Stelle-West vector; it makes that vector: the canonical tractor projected orthogonally to it has squared norm $-3/\Lambda$ and covariant derivative exactly the soldering form; the action is the curvature squared of the ambient connection contracted with the two vectors, with the frozen point's inverse norm as prefactor. Consequences, at declared levels: the functional is polynomial and defined across the singular locus; its curvature-squared presentation exists precisely when $\Lambda \neq 0$, the $\Lambda \to 0$ limit being the Einstein-Cartan functional after a topological subtraction; at a wall of the soldering form the equations never propagate a symmetric form on the wall, which on the flat model they constrain by exactly one scalar relation, while at the Schwarzschild wall the datum's connection has a simple pole whose residues, fixed by the field equations, are the weights the completion is built from; dark energy cannot evolve on the vacuum region ($w = -1$), registered against DESI and conditional off it; the forces are conformal-level while gravity alone is pre-metric; and in the neutral thermal sector of the s-wave current algebra nothing couples to the metric-forming correlations at first order except the stress-energy sector, with the $(I,V)$-sector pure gauge. Exact-arithmetic checks accompany it.

title: Tameness
(Q): joint quasi-freeness, with the s-wave weights at the half-integer offset
text:
In the stationary idealisation of the boundary modes, and for this step alone, the joint state of the mode array is taken to be the gauge-invariant quasi-free state with the marginal data that (P) and (R) (Premise \claimref{singularity.r-regularity-fixed-locus}) fix unconditionally (Theorem \claimref{singularity.rate-discharge-hypothesis-iii}, Corollary \claimref{singularity.chains-state-class-stability}): writing $\psi_k$ for the fermion modes of the array of Theorem \claimref{singularity.bosonisation-bridge-s-wave-sector}, its two-point function is $\langle \psi^\dagger_k \psi_l \rangle = \delta_{kl}\,n_k$, and every higher correlation function factorises by Wick's theorem, so that all connected correlators vanish and the joint state is KMS at $\beta = 2\pi/\kappa$ for the joint modular flow. The mode weights are evenly spaced with the array's sea level midway between two sites,
\[
\omega_k = \kappa\bigl(k + \tfrac12\bigr), \qquad k \in \Z ,
\]
so that no mode has zero weight, the weights are symmetric under the particle-hole relabelling $k \mapsto -1-k$, and the Killing flow at one modular period $2\pi/\kappa$ is the parity automorphism $\psi \mapsto -\psi$.

\emph{Why this offset.} The weights $\omega_k$ of Definition \claimref{obj.singularity.geometric-modular-condition-g} are fixed nowhere else in the framework: given (P), (R) and the quasi-free clause, an affine law $\omega_k = ck + d$ is what the currents' being normal modes of the boost flow requires, particle-hole symmetry leaves exactly two offset classes, $d = 0$ and $d = c/2$, and the slope is the value $\beta c = 2\pi$ (Theorem \claimref{synthesis.q-splits-maximum-entropy-affine-weights}(ii), (iv)). The class $d = c/2$ is adopted as a consequence of one reading, not as a bare premise: the array's modes are read as the discretised modes of the field theory's spinor fields on the horizon's light rays, $\psi(u) \mapsto e^{\kappa t/2}\psi(e^{\kappa t}u)$, of boost weight $\tfrac12$ (the weight at which the boost preserves the anticommutator), in the state that Premise \claimref{synthesis.n-plus-null-ground-state} (N$_{+}$) selects, a ground state for the affine null translations of the generators (Theorem \claimref{synthesis.positive-null-energy-gives-r-premises}). A field of boost weight $\tfrac12$ changes sign under a full turn of the regular Euclidean section, and $\kappa(k + \tfrac12)$ is the offset at which the array's Killing flow at one modular period carries that sign (Theorem \claimref{synthesis.half-integer-weight-array-carries-half-ln2}). The reading is a decision, not a derivation: the Euclidean-period sign $R_{2\pi} = -1$ (Proposition \claimref{state-selection.where-fermi-dirac-comes}) holds in a KMS state of the array at either offset, so identifying the array's real-time recurrence at one period with it is part of the reading.

\emph{On the continuum.} The joint KMS part of this premise is not a separate assumption on the continuum mode space of a horizon's generators: there it follows from (N$_{+}$), whose null ground state restricts on either side of the edge to the continuum I-state at $\beta = 2\pi/\kappa$, jointly KMS and even (Theorem \claimref{synthesis.positive-null-energy-gives-r-premises}(ii), (iii)). The stationary array statement here is its point-spectrum discretisation, on which (N$_{+}$) itself cannot be posed (part (iv) there). The quasi-free clause is a hypothesis of (N$_{+}$) as well, and (N$_{+}$) does not give the weight clause.

\emph{Consequences of the offset.} At these weights one array carries exactly $\tfrac12\ln 2$ at the Hawking temperature, given the classical theta-function identities, so under the entropy-matching hypothesis two arrays carry the capacity $\ln 2$ of one registered boundary mode with no zero-weight mode (Theorem \claimref{synthesis.half-integer-weight-array-carries-half-ln2}(i), (iii)); the current sector of one array is one oscillator tower, one helicity channel, at either offset (Theorem \claimref{synthesis.array-ln2-is-zero-mode-doublet-one-tower}(ii), (iv)), so one registered mode then corresponds to two arrays and two helicity channels. Since every mode has nonzero weight, the gluing equation of Theorem \claimref{singularity.rate-discharge-hypothesis-iii} fixes $\beta$ at every mode of the array, and the zero-weight scopes of Theorems \claimref{singularity.descended-form-state-independent}, \claimref{singularity.universality-temperature-under-g} and \claimref{singularity.rate-discharge-hypothesis-iii} do not arise on it.

\emph{Version 2.} The source states the weight clause as $\omega_k = \kappa k$ with the sea level at $k = 0$, one mode of zero weight at which the gluing equation fixes $n_0 = \tfrac12$ but not $\beta$. Results computed under that offset refer to version 2.

title: Introduction
Introduction
text:
The geometry paper of this series proves that the vacuum field equations are exactly the covariant constancy of a distinguished section of the completion's ambient bundle, the \emph{frozen point}, null for $\Lambda = 0$ and of squared norm $\Lambda/3$ otherwise \cite{ButlerT6}. That was kinematics: the equations restated. This paper is dynamics: what is gravity's action principle, in the framework's terms, and what does it permit one to do?

The answers arrange themselves around one construction. MacDowell and Mansouri showed in 1977 that gravity's action can be written as the curvature-squared functional of an (anti-)de Sitter gauge connection \cite{MacDowellMansouri1977}, broken to Lorentz symmetry, in Stelle and West's form \cite{StelleWest1980}, by an internal vector of fixed norm whose covariant derivative is the tetrad; the geometric identity of that vector has remained an interpretive puzzle for fifty years. The framework supplies the identity in two steps, and the frozen point is the first step, not the vector itself. The frozen point is parallel: that is what the vacuum equations say. So it cannot be the Stelle-West vector, whose derivative is the tetrad. What the frozen point does is reduce the ambient $SO(2,4)$-structure to the de Sitter group $SO(1,4)$, the group MacDowell and Mansouri gauge, and then, inside the de Sitter fibre, select the Stelle-West vector canonically: the canonical tractor projected orthogonally to the frozen point (Lemma \claimref{dark-energy.stelle-west-vector-frozen-point}, Theorem \claimref{dark-energy.frozen-point-makes-stelle-west-vector}). The projected vector has squared norm $-3/\Lambda$, the square of the de Sitter radius with the sign of its fibre direction, and its covariant derivative is exactly the soldering form. Gravity's dynamical principle then reads: extremise the square of the curvature as seen from the point at infinity, the frozen point supplying the reduction and the prefactor, the point at infinity's own tractor supplying the Stelle-West slot.

Five consequences, at declared levels, organise the paper. \emph{Polynomiality} (the section ``The action of the frozen point''): the functional contains no inverse metric, so it is defined wherever the ambient bundle and connection are, in particular across the singular locus where the sheaf paper's structure continues; and its curvature-squared presentation degenerates as $\Lambda \to 0$, because the prefactor is the inverse norm of the frozen point, so the presentation exists precisely because $\Lambda \neq 0$. What survives the limit, after a topological subtraction, is the Einstein-Cartan functional: the boundary is a boundary of the presentation, not of gravity's action principle, and the paper says so. \emph{Vacating} (the section ``What the equations vacate, and what cannot evolve''): at a corank-one wall of the soldering form the field equations, which polynomiality keeps meaningful there, are strictly weaker than on the invertible region, and the paper computes exactly how much weaker, at the level of the torsion, the connection and the propagation: the equations determine the connection up to one symmetric bilinear form on the wall's tangent space, which they never propagate across the wall and which, on the flat model, they constrain by a single scalar relation (the wall's Hamiltonian constraint, with the form entering as a second extrinsic curvature); the curved-wall count is posed. The sheaf paper's wall turns out to be the dual degeneration, a cometric with a radical, at which the soldering form has a pole rather than a radical; there the wall opens exactly one new gauge generator, and that generator is the boost of the completion's ladder pair. At the Schwarzschild wall the paper then computes what the frozen-point datum does: its connection has a simple pole with the Kasner residue, the field equations reach the wall as the Kasner relations on that residue, the residues are exactly the weights the sheaf paper's completion is built from, and the curvature-squared value of the action diverges through its topological term alone, a divergence a local wall counterterm removes without touching the equations; the cosmological constant leaves the residue unchanged, and the statement holds pointwise for variable exponents. The equations do not permit or demand the completion; their singularity supplies its data. \emph{Dark energy} (the section ``What the equations vacate, and what cannot evolve''): on the vacuum region the frozen point is parallel and its norm cannot evolve, $w = -1$ exactly, a maximally rigid stance registered against the DESI record; off the vacuum region the identification needs a definition the paper does not yet have, and the registration is conditional on it. \emph{Two kinds of action} (the section ``What the equations vacate, and what cannot evolve''): the MacDowell-Mansouri mechanism does not extend to the internal factors by either of its two natural routes (the ninth refutation, shared with the Standard-Model paper): the internal forces are conformal-level, gravity alone is pre-metric, and what crosses the singularity is gravity and the $\theta$-terms. \emph{One way to grip} (the section ``One way to grip: the acoustic no-go''-the section ``The engineering conclusion, and scope''): in the neutral thermal sector of the s-wave current algebra of T5, the graviton mode is the Sugawara stress tensor and nothing outside the stress-energy sector couples to it at first order; the $(I,V)$-sector is pure gauge (the point at infinity has no physical fluctuation); the four-dimensional lift inherits the orthogonality at assembly level, the sphere's operators being boundary-mode bilinears by the counting paper's theorem, conditional on that paper's Indifference premise; and the engineering conclusion holds on either reading of the graviton's ontology, by derivation inside the framework and, at leading order, by Weinberg's soft theorem outside it.

title: Prior art
text: The prior work is acknowledged once. The curvature-squared form of gravity is MacDowell-Mansouri \cite{MacDowellMansouri1977}; the symmetry-breaking internal vector is Stelle-West \cite{StelleWest1980}; the Cartan-geometric reading of both, including the contraction $\Lambda \to 0$, is Wise's \cite{Wise2010}; the almost-Einstein and scale-tractor technology is Gover's \cite{Gover2010}, and its use to read the vacuum equations is the geometry paper's \cite{ButlerT6}. The graviton-photon conversion process is Gertsenshtein's \cite{Gertsenshtein1962}. The soft-theorem universality of massless spin two is Weinberg's \cite{Weinberg1964}. The Sugawara construction and the conformal orthogonality of unequal-dimension quasi-primaries are textbook two-dimensional field theory \cite{DiFrancesco1997}. The evolving-dark-energy preference is the DESI collaboration's second data release \cite{DESI2025}, with the literature's contest recorded where it is used. What this paper claims as new is the construction of the Stelle-West vector from the frozen point and the canonical tractor, with the norm and the soldering identity proved; the across-the-locus validity of the functional; the reading of the $\Lambda \neq 0$ boundary as a boundary of the curvature-squared presentation; the exact identification of what the field equations release at a corank-one wall of the soldering form, a symmetric form on the wall that is never propagated and, on the flat model, constrained by one relation; the registered rigidity of $w$ with its condition named; the pre-metric versus conformal-level dichotomy; and the acoustic no-go stated for the thermal state in which the boundary modes lie under the singularity paper's premise (Q).

title: The Stelle-West vector of the frozen point
text:
Let a gravitational field $(\hb, \Omega)$ on flat spacetime (Definition \claimref{obj.synthesis.gtg-flat-spacetime-gauge-fields}) be Einstein with $\Lambda \neq 0$ on its invertible region, and work in the scale $g$ of its derived metric determined by the frozen point, so that $I = (1, 0, \Lambda/6) = \nInf + \tfrac{\Lambda}{6}\nO$ and $\nabla I = 0$ (Fact \claimref{dark-energy.imported-frozen-point-geometry}). Let $X := (0, 0, 1) = \nO$ be the canonical tractor, and define
\[
V \;:=\; X - \frac{\ip{X}{I}}{Q(I)}\, I \;=\; X - \frac{3}{\Lambda}\, I \;=\; \Bigl(-\frac{3}{\Lambda},\; 0,\; \frac12\Bigr),
\qquad
W \;:=\; \frac{V}{Q(V)} \;=\; \Bigl(1,\; 0,\; -\frac{\Lambda}{6}\Bigr) \;=\; \nInf - \tfrac{\Lambda}{6}\nO .
\]
Write $e_a$ for the tractor $(0, g_{ab}, 0)$, the unit vector of the $\mu_a$ slot: on flat spacetime the physical frame vector $\hb^{-1}(a)$. Then:
\begin{enumerate}
\item[(i)] $Q(X) = 0$, $\ip{X}{I} = 1$, $\ip{V}{I} = 0$, and $Q(V) = -3/\Lambda = -\ell^2$.
\item[(ii)] $\nabla_a X = e_a$, the soldering form, and $\nabla_a V = e_a$ as well; $\ip{e_a}{I} = 0$.
\item[(iii)] On a tractor with no $\mu$-component the connection \claimref{dark-energy.imported-frozen-point-geometry} acts as $\nabla_a = \partial_a + e_a\wedge W$; on a general tractor it is the Levi-Civita connection on the $\mu$-slot plus the same bivector: $\nabla_a = D_a + e_a\wedge V/Q(V)$. On flat spacetime this is the $\Cl(2,4)$ gauge field $\Omega_{T}(a) = \Omega(a) + \hb^{-1}(a) \wedge W$: the rotation-gauge field plus the soldering bivector built from the physical frame, with Schouten map $\tfrac{\Lambda}{6}\,\mathrm{id}$.
\item[(iv)] $[\,e_a\wedge W,\; e_b\wedge W\,] = -Q(W)\; e_a\wedge e_b = (\Lambda/3)\, e_a\wedge e_b$.
\end{enumerate}
proof:
Read in Gauge Theory Gravity: the metric $g$ below is the derived metric of the gravitational field $(\hb, \Omega)$ on flat spacetime, the manifold is the invertible region, and the tractor connection is a flat-space $\Cl(2,4)$ gauge field, the rotation-gauge field plus the soldering bivector; the index computation below is its reading in the splitting of $g$ (Fact \claimref{synthesis.imported-gtg-dictionary}).

(i) From $\ip{(\sigma,\mu,\rho)}{(\sigma',\mu',\rho')} \;=\; g(\mu,\mu') + \sigma\rho' + \rho\sigma'$: $Q(X) = 2\cdot 0\cdot 1 = 0$; $\ip{X}{I} = 0\cdot(\Lambda/6) + 1\cdot 1 = 1$; $\ip{V}{I} = \ip{X}{I} - (3/\Lambda)Q(I) = 1 - (3/\Lambda)(\Lambda/3) = 0$; $Q(V) = Q(X) - 2(3/\Lambda)\ip{X}{I} + (9/\Lambda^2)Q(I) = 0 - 6/\Lambda + 3/\Lambda = -3/\Lambda$. The formula for $W$ is then $V\cdot(-\Lambda/3) = (1, 0, -\Lambda/6)$.
(ii) Put $(\sigma,\mu,\rho) = (0,0,1)$ in \claimref{dark-energy.imported-frozen-point-geometry}: $\nabla_a X = (0 - 0,\; 0 + g_{ab}\cdot 1 - P_{ab}\cdot 0,\; 0 + 0) = (0, g_{ab}, 0) = e_a$, whatever $P_{ab}$ is. In the scale, $\ip{X}{I} = 1$ and $Q(I) = \Lambda/3$ are constants and $\nabla I = 0$, so $\nabla_a V = \nabla_a X = e_a$. Finally $\ip{e_a}{I} = g_{ab}\,\mu_I^b = 0$ because $\mu_I = 0$.
(iii) For $u = (\sigma,\mu,\rho)$: $\ip{W}{u} = \rho - (\Lambda/6)\sigma$ and $\ip{e_a}{u} = \mu_a$, so
$(e_a\wedge W)u = \ip{W}{u}\,e_a - \ip{e_a}{u}\,W = \bigl(-\mu_a,\; (\rho - (\Lambda/6)\sigma)\,g_{ab},\; (\Lambda/6)\,\mu_a\bigr)$,
which is exactly the non-derivative part of \claimref{dark-energy.imported-frozen-point-geometry} with $P_{ab} = (\Lambda/6)g_{ab}$; the derivative part is $\partial_a$ on the $\sigma$ and $\rho$ slots and the Levi-Civita $D_a$ on the $\mu$ slot. Since $W = V/Q(V)$ the bivector is $e_a\wedge V/Q(V)$.
(iv) For any four fibre vectors, the action convention gives $[a\wedge b, c\wedge d] = \ip{b}{c}\,a\wedge d - \ip{b}{d}\,a\wedge c - \ip{a}{c}\,b\wedge d + \ip{a}{d}\,b\wedge c$, by expanding both products on a test vector $w$ and collecting the four terms. With $a = e_a$, $b = d = W$, $c = e_b$, and $\ip{e_a}{W} = \ip{e_b}{W} = 0$, $W\wedge W = 0$, only the second term survives: $-Q(W)\,e_a\wedge e_b$, and $Q(W) = 2\cdot 1\cdot(-\Lambda/6) = -\Lambda/3$. The script confirms (i), (ii) and (iv) in exact arithmetic, and (iii) by comparing the two sides of \claimref{dark-energy.imported-frozen-point-geometry} on a basis.

title: The action of the frozen point
The frozen point makes the Stelle-West vector
proof:
Read in Gauge Theory Gravity: the metric $g$ below is the derived metric of the gravitational field $(\hb, \Omega)$ on flat spacetime, the manifold is the invertible region, and the tractor connection is the flat-space $\Cl(2,4)$ gauge field of Theorem \claimref{synthesis.gtg-tractor-gauge-field-reproduces-tractor-connection}; the index computation below is its reading in the splitting of $g$ (Fact \claimref{synthesis.imported-gtg-dictionary}).

(i) The curvature acts on $I$ by $F_{ab}\,I = [\nabla_a, \nabla_b]\,I = 0$, so at each point $F_{ab}$ lies in the stabiliser algebra of $I$. Since $Q(I) \neq 0$ the fibre splits as $\R I \oplus I^\perp$, and a bivector annihilating $I$ is a bivector of $I^\perp$ (write it in a basis adapted to the splitting: every term with an $I$ leg moves $I$). Parallel transport fixes $I$, hence preserves $I^\perp$ and the induced form on it, whose signature is $(1,4)$ or $(2,3)$ according to the sign of $\Lambda$ by Fact \claimref{dark-energy.imported-frozen-point-geometry}; so the holonomy lies in $SO(1,4)$ or $SO(2,3)$ and $\nabla$ restricts to a metric connection on $I^\perp$.
(ii) Lemma \claimref{dark-energy.stelle-west-vector-frozen-point}(i) gives $\ip{V}{I} = 0$ and $Q(V) = -3/\Lambda$; the subgroup of $SO(2,4)$ fixing both $I$ and $V$ acts on $\{I,V\}^\perp$, of signature $(2,4) - (1,0) - (0,1) = (1,3)$ for $\Lambda > 0$, where $I$ is positive and $V$ negative, and $(2,4) - (0,1) - (1,0) = (1,3)$ for $\Lambda < 0$, where they swap, and is its orthogonal group. Lemma \claimref{dark-energy.stelle-west-vector-frozen-point}(ii) gives $\nabla V = e$, Lemma \claimref{dark-energy.stelle-west-vector-frozen-point}(iii) gives the decomposition $D + e\wedge V/Q(V)$, and Lemma \claimref{dark-energy.stelle-west-vector-frozen-point}(iv) gives the quadratic term of the curvature: the bracket of the translational part with itself is $\tfrac12\cdot 2\cdot(\Lambda/3)\,e\wedge e$ in the Lorentz block, that is $\ell^{-2}e\wedge e$ with $\ell^2 = 3/\Lambda$, up to the normalisation of the bracket, while the mixed terms $[D, e\wedge V]$ carry the torsion $De$ into the translational block. This is the datum of Fact \claimref{dark-energy.imported-macdowell-mansouri-theorem-stelle-west} term by term.
(iii) On $I^\perp$ the fibre volume form is the six-dimensional volume form of $\mathcal{T}$ contracted with the unit normal $I/|I|$, and the Stelle-West contraction $\epsilon_{abcd}$ of Fact \claimref{dark-energy.imported-macdowell-mansouri-theorem-stelle-west} is that form contracted further with $V/\ell$; so $\epsilon_{abcd}F^{ab}F^{cd} = \epsilon(I, V, F, F)/(|I|\,\ell)$. Normalise with $|Q(I)|^{1/2}$ and $|Q(V)|^{1/2}$; since $Q(I)\,Q(V) = (\Lambda/3)(-3/\Lambda) = -1$ for either sign of $\Lambda$, the product of the two normalising factors is $1$ on both branches, and the Stelle-West prefactor $\ell^2 = 3/\Lambda = 1/Q(I)$ is all that remains, up to the fixed constant of the functional. The second form follows from $V = X - (3/\Lambda)I$ and the antisymmetry of $\epsilon$ in its first two slots. Slot count: six slots, two filled by $I$ and $V$, four by the two bivectors; the integrand is a scalar, which is why two vectors are needed and one is not enough.
(1) is inspection: every ingredient of $\epsilon(I, V, F, F)$, and of its value $\epsilon(I, X, F, F)$ at the canonical solution, is a section of the ambient bundle or its associated bundles, $F$ is polynomial in the connection, and no metric inverse occurs; the locators for the continuation of the bundle and the connection across the wall are those of Fact \claimref{dark-energy.imported-walls-sphere-theorem}.
(2) The pole is the rational-function statement $1/Q(I) = 3/\Lambda$, checked by the script; polynomiality of the integrand in $\Lambda$ holds because $I = (1, 0, \Lambda/6)$ and the connection \claimref{dark-energy.imported-frozen-point-geometry} are polynomial in $\Lambda$. The expansion is Fact \claimref{dark-energy.imported-macdowell-mansouri-theorem-stelle-west} with $\ell^2 = 3/\Lambda$. The interior variation of the Gauss-Bonnet term vanishes: $\delta\int\epsilon_{abcd}R^{ab}\wedge R^{cd} = 2\int\epsilon_{abcd}\,D\delta\omega^{ab}\wedge R^{cd} = 2\int d\bigl(\epsilon_{abcd}\,\delta\omega^{ab}\wedge R^{cd}\bigr) - 2\int \epsilon_{abcd}\,\delta\omega^{ab}\wedge DR^{cd}$, the first a boundary term and the second zero by the Bianchi identity $DR = 0$. The remaining two terms are polynomial in $\Lambda$, and at $\Lambda = 0$ the cosmological term vanishes, leaving the Einstein-Cartan functional, whose only ingredients are $e$, $R$ and $\epsilon_{abcd}$: no inverse of $e$ is taken, so it is defined at degenerate $e$.

title: Point of contact: why the form, not the value
text: Per the series' practice the meeting point with the cosmological-constant problem is stated where it occurs, with its limits. Theorem \claimref{dark-energy.frozen-point-makes-stelle-west-vector}(2) answers a narrower question than the one usually asked: not what value $\Lambda$ takes, and not why it is nonzero, but what its being nonzero yields. When $\Lambda \neq 0$ the frozen point has length, the ambient structure reduces to a reductive group, and gravity's action is a single curvature-squared invariant seen from the point at infinity. When $\Lambda = 0$ the frozen point is null, the prefactor $3/Q(I)$ poles, and what remains is the Einstein-Cartan functional: an action principle still, but one that no longer reads as a curvature squared and no longer sees the point at infinity. The delimiters: this is a statement about the form of the action, not about its existence; it gives no value and no smallness, and the smallness problem is not addressed and is declared so in the section ``The engineering conclusion, and scope''. That the boundary of the curvature-squared form is itself a division by zero (normalisation by a null vector, $1/Q(I)$) is, given this series' founding subject, worth recording; whether it is more than a coincidence is not something this paper can decide.

title: What the equations vacate, and what cannot evolve
The wall's free sector
text:
Let $(\hb, \Omega)$ be a gravitational field on flat spacetime (Definition \claimref{obj.synthesis.gtg-flat-spacetime-gauge-fields}) whose physical-vector map $\hb^{-1}$, here taken as the regular variable and written in an orthonormal frame $\{\gamma_a\}$ as the soldering form $e^a(v) = \gamma^a \cdot \hb^{-1}(v)$, is of corank one at a point, so that $\hb$ fails there: $e$ is a regular map $TM \to \mathbb{R}^{1,3}$ from background to physical vectors with a one-dimensional radical $r$ ($e^a(r) = 0$ for every $a$) and cokernel direction $n$ ($n_a e^a = 0$), so that the derived metric $g_{\mu\nu} = \eta_{ab}e^a_\mu e^b_\nu$ is finite and degenerate (this is the degeneration dual to the sheaf paper's; see Proposition \claimref{dark-energy.sheaf-papers-wall-soldering-variables}); the image $e(T_xM)$ is a three-dimensional subspace of the frame space, the wall's tangent space, and it may be of any type (Lorentzian, Riemannian, or null). The Einstein-Cartan equations \claimref{dark-energy.imported-macdowell-mansouri-theorem-stelle-west} are polynomial in $e$, in the rotation-gauge field written as connection one-forms $\omega$, and in their derivatives, so polynomiality (Theorem \claimref{dark-energy.frozen-point-makes-stelle-west-vector}(1)) keeps them meaningful at the point. Choose the normal form $e^a = dx^a$ for $a = 0,1,2$, $e^3 = 0$, so that $r = \partial_3$, $n = \delta^3$, and the wall's tangent space carries the frame indices $0,1,2$; write $K^{a}{}_{b} := \omega^{a}{}_{3\,b}$ and $M_{c\mu} := \tfrac12\,\epsilon_{cab}\,\omega^{ab}{}_{\mu}$ for $a, b, c, \mu \in \{0,1,2\}$, the boost components into the dying frame direction and the dualised tangential connection, and lower and raise their indices with the wall metric $\eta_{ab}$. Then:
\begin{enumerate}
\item[(a)] \emph{(Torsion.)} Regarded as linear conditions on the $24$ components of the torsion, the connection equation has rank $24$ on the invertible region and rank $18$ at the point: three of its components are identities $0 = 0$ and six torsion components are freed, all tangential to the wall (every component with a leg along $r$, and the cokernel component $n_dT^d$, are forced to vanish). Regarded as conditions on the $36$ components of the curvature, the frame equation has rank $16$ in both cases: no curvature condition is lost, and the components of the frame equation along the radical do \emph{not} vanish identically.
\item[(b)] \emph{(Connection.)} Regarded as conditions on the $24$ components of $\omega$, the connection equation has rank $12$ at the point. The free sector is exactly two symmetric tensors on the wall's tangent space: $K_{ab}$ symmetric (six components), which is invisible to the torsion because it multiplies $e^3 = 0$, and $M_{c\mu}$ symmetric (six components), which is the connection image of the freed torsion of (a), $t = (\operatorname{tr}M)\,\mathbf{1} - M$. Forced to their Levi-Civita values are the antisymmetric parts of $K$ and $M$ and every component $\omega^{ab}{}_{3}$ along the radical leg.
\item[(c)] \emph{(Propagation.)} The frame equation contains no derivative of the symmetric part of $M$ in any direction. Its principal symbol in the radical direction determines the radial derivatives $\partial_3 K_{ab}$ of all six components of $K$, and its tangential symbols impose first-order conditions on $K$ along the wall. The field equations therefore cannot propagate $M$ across the wall.
\item[(d)] \emph{(The wall's Hamiltonian constraint.)} In the normal form with $de = 0$, on the free sector $K \oplus M$ the frame equation reduces to a single component, $E_3$ evaluated on $(\partial_0, \partial_1, \partial_2)$, which reads
\[
\sigma_2'(M) \;-\; \sigma_2'(K) \;-\; 2\Lambda \;=\; 0, \qquad \sigma_2'(A) := (\operatorname{tr}A)^2 - \operatorname{tr}(A^2),
\]
with traces taken on the mixed tensors $M^{c}{}_{\mu}$, $K^{a}{}_{b}$: $K$ and $M$ enter only there, only quadratically, and with no cross term; the other fifteen components of the frame equation vanish identically on the free sector. On a curved wall the Levi-Civita part of $\omega$ adds the wall's intrinsic curvature to this component and algebraic cross terms with $M$ and $K$ to the others.
\end{enumerate}
Consequently, on the flat model of (d), the field equations at a corank-one wall of the soldering form determine the connection up to a symmetric bilinear form $M$ on the wall's tangent space which they constrain by one scalar relation and never propagate: data on the wall that the bulk equations do not determine. On a wall with intrinsic curvature the statement that survives is (c): $M$ is never propagated; how much of $M$ the fifteen other components then fix algebraically, through their cross terms with the Levi-Civita part and with the first derivatives of the connection, is a jet computation not done here (successor problem (2)). \emph{Level:} proved, for the equations as imported in Fact \claimref{dark-energy.imported-macdowell-mansouri-theorem-stelle-west}; the ranks and symbol ranks are invariant under the changes of frame and coordinates that preserve the normal form. The script confirms in exact arithmetic the counts of (a) to (c) and the single surviving component of (d) for all three types of dying direction, and the $K \oplus M$ description of (b) with the identity of (d) for the Lorentzian and Riemannian types, whose wall metric is nondegenerate; at the Riemannian type, where the boost is into a timelike direction, the cosmological term enters (d) with the opposite sign, $\sigma_2'(K) - \sigma_2'(M) - 2\Lambda = 0$. At the null type the dying direction lies in the wall, the wall metric is degenerate, and the twelve-dimensional free sector does not split as $K \oplus M$; (b) and (d) are stated for the Lorentzian normal form only. Which walls are of this type, and in particular that the sheaf paper's wall is not, is Proposition \claimref{dark-energy.sheaf-papers-wall-soldering-variables}.
proof:
Throughout, $e$ is the physical-vector map $\hb^{-1}$ in components, $e^a(v) = \gamma^a \cdot \hb^{-1}(v)$, and $\omega$ the rotation-gauge field $\Omega$ in the frame $\{\gamma_a\}$, so the component computation is one of Gauge Theory Gravity (Fact \claimref{synthesis.imported-gtg-dictionary}(i) and (ii)). \emph{Normal form.} Both equations, the Einstein-Cartan equations of \claimref{dark-energy.imported-macdowell-mansouri-theorem-stelle-west}, are built from $\epsilon_{abcd}$, $e$, $\omega$ and $d$, without the metric, which is the polynomiality of \claimref{dark-energy.frozen-point-makes-stelle-west-vector}(1). Under $GL(4)$ on the coordinates and the Lorentz group on the frame, $\epsilon_{abcd}$ is invariant up to $\det$, so ranks and symbol ranks are invariant; a corank-one $e$ may be brought to $e^a = dx^a$ ($a = 0,1,2$), $e^3 = 0$ by a coordinate change and a Lorentz rotation whenever the image is Lorentzian, to $e^0 = 0$ when it is Riemannian, and to $e^0 = e^1 = dx^0$, $e^2 = dx^2$, $e^3 = dx^3$ when it is null; the script runs all three, with identical counts, and the argument below is written for the first. Throughout, a three-form in four variables has four components, one for each omitted coordinate.

\emph{(a) Torsion, pairs not containing $3$.} For $(a,b) \in \{01, 02, 12\}$ the only nonzero terms of $\epsilon_{abcd}\,e^c\wedge T^d$ have $d = 3$, since $e^3 = 0$ removes the terms with $c = 3$; with $c$ the remaining index the equation reads $dx^c\wedge T^3 = 0$. So $T^3\wedge dx^0 = T^3\wedge dx^1 = T^3\wedge dx^2 = 0$. A two-form divisible by $dx^0$ and by $dx^1$ is a multiple of $dx^0\wedge dx^1$, and divisibility by $dx^2$ then forces it to vanish: $T^3 = 0$, six independent conditions. Each of the three equations has one component that is identically zero, the one omitting $c$: three vacated components. \emph{Pairs containing $3$.} For $(a, 3)$ with $\{b, c\} = \{0,1,2\}\setminus\{a\}$ the equation reads $dx^b\wedge T^c = dx^c\wedge T^b$. Split $T^b = \theta^b\wedge dx^3 + \tau^b$ with $\theta^b$ a one-form and $\tau^b$ a two-form in $dx^0, dx^1, dx^2$. The $dx^3$ parts give $dx^b\wedge\theta^c = dx^c\wedge\theta^b$ for all three pairs: writing $\theta^b = \theta^b_\mu dx^\mu$ and $\mu$ for the index other than $b, c$, the components are $\theta^c_\mu = 0$, $\theta^b_\mu = 0$ and $\theta^b_b + \theta^c_c = 0$; over the three pairs every off-diagonal component vanishes and $\theta^0_0 + \theta^1_1 = \theta^0_0 + \theta^2_2 = \theta^1_1 + \theta^2_2 = 0$, so $\theta = 0$: nine conditions, every radical-leg component gone. The $dx^3$-free parts give $dx^b\wedge\tau^c = dx^c\wedge\tau^b$, one condition per pair, three in all, on the nine components of $\tau$: six free, all tangential. Total rank $6 + 9 + 3 = 18$; on the invertible region the same argument with all four $dx^a$ present is the classical one and gives $T = 0$, rank $24$. \emph{Frame equation.} With $e^3 = 0$,
\[
\begin{aligned}
E_3 &= \epsilon_{3bcd}\,dx^b\wedge F^{cd} \qquad (b,c,d \in \{0,1,2\}),\\
E_a &= 2\sum_{b,c}\epsilon_{abc3}\,dx^b\wedge F^{c3} \qquad (a \in \{0,1,2\};\ b, c \in \{0,1,2\}\setminus\{a\}).
\end{aligned}
\]
The unknowns separate: $F^{01}, F^{02}, F^{12}$ enter only $E_3$, and $F^{03}, F^{13}, F^{23}$ enter only $E_0, E_1, E_2$. For $E_3$, the four choices $F^{12} = dx^1\wedge dx^2$, $dx^1\wedge dx^3$, $dx^2\wedge dx^3$ and $F^{02} = dx^2\wedge dx^3$ produce, one each, the four components of a three-form: rank $4$. For $E_0, E_1, E_2$ split $F^{c3} = \phi^c\wedge dx^3 + \psi^c$. The $dx^3$-leg components are $\epsilon_{abc}\,dx^b\wedge\phi^c$, nine from nine, and this map is the $\theta$ system above with the roles renamed, hence bijective; the $dx^3$-free components, one per $E_a$, are hit independently by $\psi^2_{02}$, $\psi^0_{01}$ and $\psi^1_{12}$. Rank $4 + 9 + 3 = 16$, the full target; on the invertible region rank can only be at least as large and the target is sixteen-dimensional. For the radical components, $\iota_r E_a = -\epsilon_{abcd}\,e^b\wedge\iota_r F^{cd}$ is not zero for generic $F$; the script exhibits an integer instance.

\emph{(b) Connection.} An inhomogeneous $de^a$ enters the connection equation only as a source term, which leaves the rank of the linear map $\omega \mapsto \epsilon\,e\wedge T(\omega)$ unchanged, so take $de = 0$: $T^a = \omega^{a}{}_{b}\wedge e^b$. The dying direction: $T^3 = \sum_{b<3}\omega^{3}{}_{b\mu}\,dx^\mu\wedge dx^b$, whose tangential components are the antisymmetric part of $\omega^{3}{}_{b\mu}$ in $(b,\mu)$ and whose radial-leg components are $\omega^{3}{}_{b3}$; $T^3 = 0$ therefore forces the antisymmetric part of $K$ and the three components $\omega^{a3}{}_{3}$ to vanish and leaves the symmetric part of $K$ free, six components; $K$ never enters $T^a$ for $a < 3$, because there it multiplies $e^3 = 0$. The tangential connection: for $a < 3$, $T^a = \omega^{a}{}_{b}\wedge dx^b$ over $b < 3$, so $T^a_{\,3n} = \omega^{a}{}_{n3}$ and the radical-leg condition $\theta = 0$ of (a) forces $\omega^{ab}{}_{3} = 0$, three components; and $T^a_{\,mn} = \omega^{a}{}_{nm} - \omega^{a}{}_{mn}$ for $m,n < 3$ is the classical three-dimensional torsion-contortion map, a bijection of nine-dimensional spaces. Dualising with $\omega^{ab}{}_{\mu} = \epsilon^{abc}M_{c\mu}$ and $t^{a}{}_{d} = \tfrac12\epsilon_{d}{}^{mn}T^a_{\,mn}$, the contraction $\epsilon_{dmn}\epsilon^{amc} = \delta^a_d\delta^c_n - \delta^c_d\delta^a_n$ gives $t = (\operatorname{tr}M)\mathbf{1} - M$, so $t$ is symmetric exactly when $M$ is: the three conditions of (a) are the vanishing of the antisymmetric part of $M$, and the free sector is the symmetric part, six components. Forced: three from each of the antisymmetric part of $K$, the radial-leg $\omega^{a3}{}_{3}$, the radial-leg $\omega^{ab}{}_{3}$ and the antisymmetric part of $M$: rank $12$, free $12$, as claimed.

\emph{(c) Propagation.} The derivative terms of the frame equation are $\epsilon_{abcd}\,e^b\wedge d\omega^{cd}$. For $a = 3$ and $b < 3$ the pair $(c,d)$ is the complement of $b$ in $\{0,1,2\}$, so $\omega^{cd}$ is $\pm M_{b\mu}$: the components of $E_3$ with a $dx^3$ leg are $\partial_3(M_{bx} - M_{xb})$ up to sign, the antisymmetric part only, and the component without a $dx^3$ leg is $\epsilon^{bmn}\partial_m M_{bn}$ up to sign, which vanishes on symmetric $M$. So no derivative of symmetric $M$ appears in $E_3$, and none appears in $E_a$ for $a < 3$, where only $\omega^{c3}$, that is $K$ and its forced complement, occurs. For $K$: the $dx^3$-leg components of $E_a$ ($a < 3$) are $\partial_3 K_{c y}$ with $c$ the index other than $a, b$ and $y \neq b$, which over the two choices of $b$ and the allowed $y$ reach all six components of symmetric $K$; the remaining components carry tangential derivatives of $K$. The script confirms the symbol ranks: $0$ on $M$ in every direction, $6$ on $K$ in the radial direction and $3$ in each tangential direction.

\emph{(d) The Hamiltonian component.} With $de = 0$ and the forced sector at its Levi-Civita value zero, $R^{cd} = \omega^{c}{}_{f}\wedge\omega^{fd}$ and the frame equation is quadratic in $(K, M)$. For $a < 3$ every term of $E_a$ carries $\omega^{c3}$ against $\omega^{3d}$ or a tangential $\omega$, and the $dx^3$-free components need three tangential legs from two one-forms and $dx^b$, which is impossible with $b$ fixed by $a$; the script confirms that all twelve components of $E_a$, $a<3$, vanish identically on the free sector. For $E_3$ on $(\partial_0,\partial_1,\partial_2)$: the $f = 3$ terms give $\epsilon_{3bcd}\,dx^b\wedge\omega^{c}{}_{3}\wedge\omega^{3d} = -\epsilon_{bcd}\,\epsilon^{bxy}K^{c}{}_{x}K^{d}{}_{y} = -\bigl(\delta^x_c\delta^y_d - \delta^x_d\delta^y_c\bigr)K^{c}{}_{x}K^{d}{}_{y} = -\sigma_2'(K)$, and the $f < 3$ terms give, after dualising both factors with $\omega^{cd} = \epsilon^{cdg}M_{g\mu}$, the same contraction on $M$ with the opposite sign, $+\sigma_2'(M)$; cross terms vanish because $\omega^{c}{}_{3}\wedge\omega^{3d}$ and $\omega^{c}{}_{f}\wedge\omega^{fd}$ ($f<3$) lie in different terms. The cosmological term $\ell^{-2}\epsilon_{3bcd}\,e^b\wedge e^c\wedge e^d$ contributes $-6\ell^{-2} = -2\Lambda$ on $(\partial_0,\partial_1,\partial_2)$. The script confirms the identity $E_3(\partial_0,\partial_1,\partial_2) = \sigma_2'(M) - \sigma_2'(K)$ on random elements of the free sector, the vanishing of the cross term, and the coefficient $-6$.

title: $w = -1$ on the vacuum region; the registration, and its condition
proof:
Read in Gauge Theory Gravity: the metric $g$ below is the derived metric of the gravitational field $(\hb, \Omega)$ on flat spacetime, the manifold is the invertible region, and the tractor connection is the flat-space $\Cl(2,4)$ gauge field of Theorem \claimref{synthesis.gtg-tractor-gauge-field-reproduces-tractor-connection}; the index computation below is its reading in the splitting of $g$ (Fact \claimref{synthesis.imported-gtg-dictionary}).

(i) is the displayed computation. For its sign: in the store's convention the Einstein equation with source $T$ and no cosmological constant is $\Ric + 8\pi G\,T = 4\pi G\,(g^{ab}T_{ab})\,g$; with the source $T + c\,g$ this becomes $\Ric + 8\pi G\,T = (8\pi G\,c + 4\pi G\,g^{ab}T_{ab})\,g$, which is the equation with cosmological constant $\Lambda$ exactly when $c = \Lambda/8\pi G$ (for $T = 0$ it is $\Ric = \Lambda g$, de Sitter for $\Lambda > 0$). For a unit timelike $u$ ($Q(u) = 1$) the energy density is $T^{\Lambda}(u, u) = \Lambda/8\pi G$, and for a unit spacelike $e$ ($Q(e) = -1$) orthogonal to it the pressure is $T^{\Lambda}(e, e) = -\Lambda/8\pi G$, reading $T = (\rho + p)\,u\otimes u - p\,g$; so $p = -\rho$. (ii): by \claimref{dark-energy.imported-frozen-point-geometry}, for $I_g = (1, 0, J/4)$ the $\sigma$ slot of $\nabla_a I_g$ is $0 - 0 = 0$, the $\rho$ slot is $\tfrac14\partial_a J + P_a{}^b\cdot 0 = \tfrac14\partial_a J$, and the $\mu$ slot is $0 + (J/4)g_{ab} - P_{ab}$, minus the trace-free Schouten tensor. The $\mu$ slot vanishes if and only if $P_{ab}$ is pure trace, that is if and only if $g$ is Einstein; and an Einstein four-metric has constant scalar curvature by the contracted Bianchi identity, hence constant $J$, so the $\rho$ slot vanishes with it. Thus $\nabla I_g = 0$ exactly when $g$ is Einstein. The norm is $\ip{(\sigma,\mu,\rho)}{(\sigma',\mu',\rho')} \;=\; g(\mu,\mu') + \sigma\rho' + \rho\sigma'$: $Q(I_g) = 2\cdot 1\cdot J/4 = J/2$, and $J = R/6$ in four dimensions. The script confirms the $\mu$ slot on an exact non-Einstein instance and on an Einstein one, and the $\rho$ slot $\tfrac14\partial_a J$ on an instance with non-constant $J$. (iii) is a registration, not a computation; its hypothesis rests on \claimref{dark-energy.frozen-point-makes-stelle-west-vector}, in which the cosmological constant enters the action as the norm $Q(I) = \Lambda/3$ of the frozen point.

title: Gravity is pre-metric; the forces degenerate exactly where the conformal class does
proof: (1) Internal invariance of $I$ is structural: $I$ is a section of the tractor factor and the internal groups act on the internal factor, and $F_i$ is a two-form with values in the internal Lie algebra, with no tractor slot for $\epsilon$ or $I$ to contract. Topologicality: $d\,\tr(F\wedge F) = \tr(DF\wedge F) + \tr(F\wedge DF) = 2\tr(DF\wedge F) = 0$ by the Bianchi identity $DF = 0$, using that two-forms commute under the wedge and the trace is cyclic; locally $\tr(F\wedge F) = d(\mathrm{CS}(A))$, and the variation $\delta\int\tr(F\wedge F) = 2\int\tr(D\delta A\wedge F) = 2\int d\,\tr(\delta A\wedge F) - 2\int\tr(\delta A\wedge DF)$ is a boundary term plus zero: no field equations. (2) The star on two-forms in four dimensions is $*\alpha_{ab} = \tfrac12\sqrt{|g|}\,\epsilon_{abcd}\,g^{ce}g^{df}\alpha_{ef}$; under $g \mapsto \Omega^2 g$ the factor $\sqrt{|g|}$ scales by $\Omega^4$ and the two inverse metrics by $\Omega^{-4}$, so $*$ is invariant: it depends on $[g]$ only, and not on the scale that the frozen point fixes. It does depend on $[g]$: with $g$ degenerate, $g^{-1}$ does not exist. Gravity's action, by contrast, contains no inverse metric (\claimref{dark-energy.frozen-point-makes-stelle-west-vector}(1)). (3) is (2) read at a corank-one wall, where the cometric $g^{ce}$ has a one-dimensional radical and $\sqrt{|g|}$ a half-power pole (Fact \claimref{dark-energy.imported-walls-sphere-theorem}), for every representative of the conformal class alike, so $*$ on two-forms is not a nondegenerate map there; the $\theta$-terms $\theta\int\tr(F\wedge F)$ are star-free, hence cross. The trace identities used in (1) are confirmed by the script on exact instances; they are the only computational content.

title: Point of contact: what the dichotomy explains
text: The theorem answers questions it was not asked, and the series keeps them in view per its practice: why gravity is universal (it is the one force whose action needs no metric); why it alone resists quantisation-as-a-force (it was never a force in the sense the others are: its action is pre-metric while theirs are conformal-level); and what survives the singularity (gravity, and the strong-CP parameter, which crosses). What the dichotomy does not determine, and what this paper does not supply: the three coupling normalisations $g_i$, the condensation data, and the chirality of the weak coupling, which are the task of the matter papers, the mass paper T11 \cite{ButlerT11} and the standard-model paper T12 \cite{ButlerT12}.

title: Which wall: the soldering form against the sheaf paper's degeneration
text: Theorem \claimref{dark-energy.walls-free-sector} is a theorem about a soldering form with a radical: $g_{\mu\nu} = \eta_{ab}e^a_\mu e^b_\nu$ degenerate, the metric on tangent vectors acquiring a null direction. The sheaf paper's tame wall is a degeneration of the \emph{cometric}, the form on covectors, and the two are not the same degeneration. The following proposition records exactly how they differ, what the sheaf paper's wall looks like in soldering variables, and which piece of the completion the wall's extra freedom is.

title: The sheaf paper's wall in soldering variables
text:

title: What this settles, and what it reformulates
text: Two things are settled. The symmetric form $M$ of Theorem \claimref{dark-energy.walls-free-sector} is the free sector of a wall of the soldering form, the degeneration dual to the sheaf paper's, and it is not the completion's sector at the sheaf paper's wall; the claim that the sheaf paper's wall is a wall of the soldering form is withdrawn. And the completion's ladder pair does appear in the dynamics at the sheaf paper's wall, but as gauge, not as a field: the wall opens exactly one new gauge generator per point, the dilation of the dying line, and that generator is the boost of the ladder plane $\mathrm{span}(k, k^*)$. The half-power weight that the sheaf paper's residue theorem assigns to $k$ ($\mathcal{L}^{\otimes 2} \cong N^*\Sigma$) is a particular gauge choice for this generator, the one that makes the exceptional algebra nondegenerate. What is reformulated is the dynamical question: whether the equations demand the completion becomes, at the sheaf paper's wall, the question of how the MacDowell-Mansouri datum fails to extend, and the section ``The interface at the Schwarzschild wall: the datum has a pole, and its residue is the completion's weight'' answers it for the Schwarzschild wall: the datum's connection has a simple pole, and the residues of that pole are the weights from which the completion is built.

title: The interface at the Schwarzschild wall: the datum has a pole, and its residue is the completion's weight
text: Proposition \claimref{dark-energy.sheaf-papers-wall-soldering-variables}(iv) left one question: whether the MacDowell-Mansouri datum $(\nabla, I, X)$ extends regularly across the sheaf paper's wall. For the Schwarzschild singularity the geometry and sheaf papers between them already contain the answer, and this subsection extracts it and computes what it does to the action.

title: Imported: the weighted limit at the Schwarzschild singularity, and its matching
text: For the Schwarzschild interior gravitational field $(\hb, \Omega)$ on flat spacetime (Definition \claimref{obj.synthesis.gtg-flat-spacetime-gauge-fields}) in synchronous time $\tau$ (with $\tau = 0$ the singularity), and equally for the Schwarzschild-de Sitter interior field, the functions of whose derived metric differ by relative $O(\Lambda\tau^2)$ and for which the same limit holds with the same exponents and rates \cite[Thm.~5.9]{ButlerT6}, the orthonormal physical frame adapted to the Killing and sphere directions is $D$-parallel along the free-fall worldlines of velocity $g_\tau$, and the connection is Kasner at leading order: the Hubble-normalised connection $\tau\,\omega$, with $\omega(A) = \Omega(\hb(A))$ the rotation-gauge field on physical vectors, tends to $-\sum_i p_i\, B_i \otimes \hat\theta^i$ with $B_i$ the boosts (the sign of the Definition, in which the Cartan forms $\omega^i{}_0 = \sigma_i\theta^i$ assemble to $-\sigma_i B_i$), $\hat\theta^i$ the normalised coframe, and exponents $(p_1, p_2, p_3) = (-\tfrac13, \tfrac23, \tfrac23)$, with explicit rates: $O(\tau^{2/3})$ in the boost block and $O(\tau^{1/3})$ in the rotation block, the latter being the sphere's own connection, which is outside the Kasner comparison; the limit is a values-level statement (the algebra generated by the limiting connection values); the transport-level statement, convergence of the transport to the Kasner model's transport, holds along every tangential curve of fixed Hubble-normalised length, for every admissible gravitational field of the geometry paper's class \cite[Def.~5.5]{ButlerT6}, whose exponents satisfy $\sum_i p_i^2 = 1$ \cite[Thm.~5.11]{ButlerT6}, and along the Schwarzschild $\varphi$-lines exactly, at rate $\tau^{1/3}$ \cite[Cor.~5.12]{ButlerT6}; what the geometry paper disclaims is the comparison over segments of fixed coordinate length, whose Hubble-normalised length diverges, and about which no claim is made here either. This coframe consists of sections of the sheaf paper's exceptional module, the weights of the sheaf paper's completion are forced to equal the exponents, and the total residue bivector $B_w = \sum_i p_i\, \hat e_0\wedge\hat e_i$ is a unit boost of the exceptional algebra. \emph{Provenance:} \cite[Lems.~5.1-5.4, Def.~5.5, Thm.~5.6, Thm.~5.9, Thm.~5.11, Cor.~5.12]{ButlerT6}; \cite[Thm.~8.16, Prop.~8.26, Thm.~8.27]{ButlerT4}.
proof:
The collected statements are read in Gauge Theory Gravity through Fact \claimref{synthesis.imported-gtg-dictionary}: the frame is the physical frame of the gravitational field, its parallelism is $D$-parallelism, and the connection is the rotation-gauge field. In the Schwarzschild interior in synchronous time $\tau$ (with $\tau = 0$ the singularity), and equally in the Schwarzschild-de Sitter interior, whose metric functions differ by relative $O(\Lambda\tau^2)$ and for which the same limit holds with the same exponents and rates \cite[Thm.~5.9]{ButlerT6} (\claimref{interior.schwarzschild-de-sitter-weighted-limit}), the orthonormal frame adapted to the Killing and sphere directions is parallel along $\partial_\tau$, and its connection is Kasner at leading order: the Hubble-normalised connection $\tau\,\omega$ tends to $-\sum_i p_i\, B_i \otimes \hat\theta^i$ with $B_i$ the boosts, $\hat\theta^i$ the normalised coframe, and exponents $(p_1, p_2, p_3) = (-\tfrac13, \tfrac23, \tfrac23)$, with explicit rates: $O(\tau^{2/3})$ in the boost block and $O(\tau^{1/3})$ in the rotation block, the latter being the sphere's own connection, which is outside the Kasner comparison; the limit is a values-level statement (the algebra generated by the limiting connection values); the transport-level statement, convergence of the transport to the Kasner model's transport, holds along every tangential curve of fixed Hubble-normalised length, for every admissible metric of the geometry paper's class \cite[Def.~5.5]{ButlerT6}, whose exponents satisfy $\sum_i p_i^2 = 1$ \cite[Thm.~5.11]{ButlerT6} (\claimref{interior.transport-level-convergence-along-tangential-curves}), and along the Schwarzschild $\varphi$-lines exactly, at rate $\tau^{1/3}$ \cite[Cor.~5.12]{ButlerT6} (\claimref{interior.schwarzschild-lines-exactly}); what the geometry paper disclaims is the comparison over segments of fixed coordinate length, whose Hubble-normalised length diverges, and about which no claim is made here either. This coframe consists of sections of the sheaf paper's exceptional module, the weights of the sheaf paper's completion are forced to equal the exponents, and the total residue bivector $B_w = \sum_i p_i\, \hat e_0\wedge\hat e_i$ is a unit boost of the exceptional algebra. \emph{Provenance:} \cite[Lems.~5.1-5.4, Def.~5.5, Thm.~5.6, Thm.~5.9, Thm.~5.11, Cor.~5.12]{ButlerT6} (\claimref{interior.kasner-form-interior}, \claimref{interior.weighted-limit-theorem}, \claimref{interior.boosts-generate-exactly-levi-factor}); \cite[Thm.~8.16, Prop.~8.26, Thm.~8.27]{ButlerT4} (\claimref{sheaf.matching-connection-level}, \claimref{sheaf.matching-fibre}, \claimref{sheaf.weights-are-forced-are-kasner-exponents}).

This restates \claimref{interior.exact-parallelism-convergence-rate}, \claimref{interior.interior-connection-exactly}.

title: The cosmological constant does not change the residue
text:
Let $(\hb, \Omega)$ be a diagonal Bianchi I gravitational field on flat spacetime (Definition \claimref{obj.synthesis.gtg-flat-spacetime-gauge-fields}), with derived metric $g = d\tau^2 - \sum_i a_i(\tau)^2(dx^i)^2$ and Hubble rates $H_i = \dot a_i/a_i$, so that on the orthonormal physical frame $\{\gamma_0, \gamma_i\}$ over $(\partial_\tau, \partial_i)$ the rotation-gauge field is $\Omega(\gamma_i) = -H_i\,\gamma_0 \wedge \gamma_i$, $\Omega(\gamma_0) = 0$ (as Levi-Civita connection forms of $g$ in the coframe $e^i = a_i\,dx^i$, $\omega^{i0} = H_i\,e^i$), and impose the vacuum field equations with cosmological constant, $\mathcal{R}(a) = \Lambda a$ in the store's sign (for the derived metric, $\mathrm{Ric} = \Lambda g$):
\[
\dot H_i + H_i\sum_j H_j = \Lambda \quad (i = 1,2,3), \qquad \sum_{i<j}H_iH_j = \Lambda .
\]
Then for every Kasner point $(p_1, p_2, p_3)$ there is a unique formal solution with a simple pole of residue $p$ at $\tau = 0$, and it is odd in $\tau$ with regular corrections:
\[
H_i \;=\; \frac{p_i}{\tau} \;+\; \frac{\Lambda}{2}\,(1 - p_i)\,\tau \;+\; \sum_{n \geq 2} h_{i,n}\,\tau^{2n-1},
\]
every $h_{i,n}$ a polynomial in $\Lambda$ and $p$ determined by the evolution equations alone, the constraint then holding identically. In the Bianchi I class the first correction to the connection is therefore $O(\Lambda\tau)$ and regular. At a Schwarzschild-de Sitter wall, whose slices are Kantowski-Sachs rather than flat, the sphere's intrinsic curvature adds corrections of relative order $\tau^{1/3}$ in the rotation block and $\tau^{2/3}$ in the boost block (Fact \claimref{dark-energy.imported-weighted-limit-schwarzschild-singularity-matching}), larger than $\Lambda\tau^2$ and singular in absolute terms; what this proposition establishes there is only that the residue, the coefficient of $\tau^{-1}$, is the Kasner boost of the $\Lambda = 0$ approach and that the field equations at the wall remain the Kasner relations.
proof: Substitute $H_i = p_i/\tau + \sum_{n\geq 1}h_{i,n}\tau^{2n-1}$. At order $\tau^{-2}$ the evolution equations give $-p_i + p_i\sum_j p_j = 0$ and the constraint gives $\sum_{i<j}p_ip_j = 0$: the Kasner relations. At order $\tau^{2n-2}$, $n \geq 1$, the evolution equation for $i$ reads $(2n-1)h_{i,n} + h_{i,n}\sum_j p_j + p_i\sum_j h_{j,n} = \Lambda\,\delta_{n,1} - K_{i,n}$, where $K_{i,n}$ collects the products of coefficients already determined; with $\sum p = 1$ this is $2n\,h_{i,n} + p_i\,\mathcal{H}_n = \Lambda\delta_{n,1} - K_{i,n}$ with $\mathcal{H}_n := \sum_j h_{j,n}$. Summing over $i$ gives $(2n+1)\mathcal{H}_n = 3\Lambda\delta_{n,1} - \sum_iK_{i,n}$, which determines $\mathcal{H}_n$ and then each $h_{i,n}$ uniquely. For $n = 1$, $K_{i,1} = 0$, so $\mathcal{H}_1 = \Lambda$ and $h_{i,1} = (\Lambda - p_i\Lambda)/2$. Odd powers only: no even power of $\tau$ is sourced, since the equations are quadratic in $H$ with the pole at odd order and $\Lambda$ at order zero. The constraint is preserved by the evolution: with $S := \sum_iH_i$ and $C := \sum_{i<j}H_iH_j$ the evolution equations give $\dot C = 2S(\Lambda - C)$, so $C - \Lambda$ obeys a linear homogeneous equation whose solutions near $\tau = 0$ behave as $\tau^{-2}$, and the Kasner relation $\sum_{i<j}p_ip_j = 0$ sets that mode's coefficient to zero; the constraint therefore holds to all orders once it holds at the pole. Odd powers only is likewise forced: an even power $c_i\tau^{2n}$ in $H_i$, $n \geq 0$, would enter the evolution equations at order $\tau^{2n-1}$, where nothing sources it, through three terms, $2n\,c_i$ from $\dot H_i$, $c_i\sum_jp_j = c_i$ from $c_i\tau^{2n}$ against the pole of $\sum_jH_j$, and $p_i\sum_jc_j$ from the pole of $H_i$ against $\sum_jc_j\tau^{2n}$; the system $(2n+1)c_i + p_i\sum_jc_j = 0$ sums to $(2n+2)\sum_jc_j = 0$, hence $\sum_jc_j = 0$ and $c_i = 0$; the script confirms this by direct substitution to order $\tau^4$ at the Schwarzschild exponents with $\Lambda = 3$, where $h_{i,1} = (2, \tfrac12, \tfrac12)$, $h_{i,2} = (-\tfrac{33}{20}, -\tfrac{3}{40}, -\tfrac{3}{40})$, and both residuals vanish identically through the order computed. The Schwarzschild-de Sitter interior is not in this class (its slices are Kantowski-Sachs); what the geometry paper's Theorem 5.9 \cite[Thm.~5.9]{ButlerT6} (\claimref{interior.schwarzschild-de-sitter-weighted-limit}) gives is that it shares the residue and the exponents of the Schwarzschild approach, with the same weighted limit and rates (\claimref{dark-energy.imported-weighted-limit-schwarzschild-singularity-matching}), which is all the statement claims for it.

title: The frozen-point datum at a Kasner wall
text:
Let $g = d\tau^2 - \sum_i a_i(\tau)^2(dx^i)^2$ be the derived metric of the synchronous diagonal gravitational field on flat spacetime with $\hb^{-1}(e_\tau) = e_\tau$, $\hb^{-1}(e_i) = a_i e_i$ (Definition \claimref{obj.synthesis.gtg-flat-spacetime-gauge-fields}), a solution of the Einstein equations with cosmological constant $\Lambda \neq 0$ in the diagonal Bianchi I class of Proposition \claimref{dark-energy.cosmological-constant-does-not-change-residue}, with residue $(p_1,p_2,p_3)$ at $\tau = 0$ and $p_1p_2p_3 \neq 0$ (which excludes exactly the permutations of $(1,0,0)$, the flat Milne point, where every curvature below vanishes and the pole is a coordinate horizon), so that $a_i = \tau^{p_i}(1 + O(\Lambda\tau^2))$ and the Kasner metric $d\tau^2 - \sum_i\tau^{2p_i}(dx^i)^2$ is its leading term; let $e^0 = d\tau$, $e^i = a_i\,dx^i$ be the orthonormal coframe (the physical frame of the field read as one-forms), and let the ambient datum be that of Theorem \claimref{dark-energy.frozen-point-makes-stelle-west-vector}: $I = (1, 0, \Lambda/6)$, $X = (0,0,1)$, and $\nabla$ the tractor connection \claimref{dark-energy.imported-frozen-point-geometry} of $g$ (on flat spacetime the $\Cl(2,4)$ gauge field $\Omega_{T}$ of Theorem \claimref{synthesis.gtg-tractor-gauge-field-reproduces-tractor-connection}), whose Schouten tensor is $P_{ab} = (\Lambda/6)g_{ab}$ because $g$ is Einstein. (An exact Kasner metric is Ricci-flat and carries the null frozen point of $\Lambda = 0$. The statements of (i) and (ii) and the Gauss-Bonnet density of (iii) are computed on the leading Kasner term, with $\Lambda$ entering only through the Schouten summand, and hold verbatim for the exact Kasner metric at $\Lambda = 0$, the Schwarzschild exponents included; $\Lambda \neq 0$ is needed only for the statements about the curvature-squared form of the action, which are made on the Einstein family.) Then, in the orthonormal frame, which for the Schwarzschild-de Sitter interior is the sheaf paper's exceptional chart (Fact \claimref{dark-energy.imported-weighted-limit-schwarzschild-singularity-matching} with Proposition \claimref{dark-energy.cosmological-constant-does-not-change-residue}), at leading order in $\tau$:
\begin{enumerate}
\item[(i)] \emph{(What is regular, and what is not.)} $I$ and $X$ are constant sections of constant norm, the soldering form $\nabla_a X = e_a$ is regular of full rank, and the soldering and Schouten summands of $\nabla$ are the constant matrices $\eta_{ab}$ and $(\Lambda/6)\eta_{ab}$. The only singular part of the datum is the Levi-Civita block, and its leading term is a simple pole:
\[
\omega^{i0} \;=\; \frac{p_i}{\tau}\, e^i, \qquad \omega^{ij} = 0 ,
\]
with residue, read as the rotation-gauge field of the Definition (whose sign, $D_a = a \cdot \nabla + \Omega(a) \times$, takes the Cartan forms $\omega^{i0}$ to minus the boosts), the bivector-valued one-form $-\sum_i p_i\,B_i\otimes \hat e^i$, $B_i = e_0\wedge e_i$, whose legs are tangential to the wall. It is not a gauge pole: its curvature is a double pole,
\[
R^{i0} \;=\; \frac{p_i(p_i - 1)}{\tau^2}\, e^0\wedge e^i, \qquad R^{ij} \;=\; -\frac{p_i p_j}{\tau^2}\, e^i\wedge e^j .
\]
The datum therefore does not extend regularly across the wall in this chart, and in no chart: the Euler density of (iii) equals $\sqrt{|g|}$ times the Kretschmann scalar on an Einstein metric, because $-4R_{ab}R^{ab} + R^2 = -16\Lambda^2 + 16\Lambda^2 = 0$, so the Kretschmann scalar is $-16p_1p_2p_3\tau^{-4}$ at leading order, divergent when $p_1p_2p_3 \neq 0$, and a curvature scalar is chart-independent.
\item[(ii)] \emph{(The field equations at the wall are conditions on the residue.)} In the curvature convention of the geometry paper, in which de Sitter has $\mathrm{Ric}_{ab} = \Lambda g_{ab}$ and $P_{ab} = (\Lambda/6)g_{ab}$ (the convention that makes $I$ parallel), the Ricci tensor in the frame is diagonal with
\[
\tau^2 R_{00} = \sum_i p_i^2 - \sum_i p_i, \qquad \tau^2 R_{ii} = -\,p_i\Bigl(\sum_j p_j - 1\Bigr) ,
\]
so the vacuum equations at leading order are exactly the Kasner relations $\sum_i p_i = 1 = \sum_i p_i^2$; the second says that the residue bivector $-B_w$, with $B_w = \sum_i p_i B_i$, is a unit boost. With $\Lambda$ the Einstein-$\Lambda$ system of Proposition \claimref{dark-energy.cosmological-constant-does-not-change-residue} replaces Ricci-flatness at relative order $\Lambda\tau^2$ and does not affect the residue.
\item[(iii)] \emph{(The action at the wall.)} On the Kasner approach the three terms of Theorem \claimref{dark-energy.frozen-point-makes-stelle-west-vector}(2) have densities
\[
\begin{aligned}
\epsilon_{abcd}R^{ab}\wedge R^{cd} &= -16\,p_1p_2p_3\;\tau^{-3}\, d\tau\wedge d^3x, \\
\epsilon_{abcd}\,e^a e^b R^{cd} &= O(\Lambda\,\tau)\, d\tau\wedge d^3x, \qquad
\epsilon_{abcd}\,e^ae^be^ce^d = 24\,\tau\, d\tau\wedge d^3x .
\end{aligned}
\]

title: The forcing half at the Schwarzschild wall, in the residue sense
text:
The steps, each with its provenance:
\begin{enumerate}
\item \emph{(The datum's pole.)} At the singular locus $r = 0$ of the Schwarzschild gravitational field on flat spacetime (Definition \claimref{obj.synthesis.gtg-flat-spacetime-gauge-fields}) the frozen-point datum is regular in the exceptional chart except for a simple pole of the connection in its Levi-Civita block, the rotation-gauge field $\Omega$, with tangential legs, residue $-\sum_i p_iB_i\otimes\hat e^i$ (the sign of the Definition): Proposition \claimref{dark-energy.frozen-point-datum-kasner-wall}(i) on the Kasner model, transported to Schwarzschild by Fact \claimref{dark-energy.imported-weighted-limit-schwarzschild-singularity-matching} (the geometry paper's weighted limit, values-level, with its $O(\tau^{2/3})$ corrections in the boost block and $O(\tau^{1/3})$ in the rotation block).
\item \emph{(The residues satisfy the wall's field equations.)} The exponents obey the Kasner relations, which are the leading-order field equations, and the second relation is the statement that the residue bivector is a unit boost: Proposition \claimref{dark-energy.frozen-point-datum-kasner-wall}(ii), \cite[Prop.~8.26(3)]{ButlerT4}.
\item \emph{(The residues are the completion's weights.)} The sheaf paper's completion at this wall is built on weights that are forced, once the dying direction is named, to equal the Kasner exponents: \cite[Thm.~8.16]{ButlerT4}; and its exceptional frame is the frame in which (1) holds: \cite[Thm.~8.27]{ButlerT4}.
\end{enumerate}
Consequently, at this wall, the field equations neither merely permit the completion nor demand it as a further condition: their own singular locus supplies the data the completion is built from. The pole of the dynamical connection is not removable (step 1), its residues are fixed by the equations (step 2), and those residues are the weights of the completion (step 3). This is the forcing half of the section ``What the equations vacate, and what cannot evolve'' answered in the residue sense. Three qualifications are discharged below: the cosmological corrections leave the residue unchanged (Proposition \claimref{dark-energy.cosmological-constant-does-not-change-residue}); the divergent curvature-squared \emph{value} is removed by a local wall counterterm that does not change the equations (Proposition \claimref{dark-energy.wall-counterterm}); and the residue statement holds pointwise for variable exponents in the diagonal class (Lemma \claimref{dark-energy.variable-exponents-residue-pointwise-corrections-are}), with the momentum constraints and the non-diagonal class remaining as the dynamical half of the sheaf paper's connection-level matching \cite[Rem.~8.28]{ButlerT4}.

title: The wall counterterm
text:
Assume $\Lambda \neq 0$, so that the curvature-squared form (quadratic in the field strength) exists. Let $\omega^{ab}$ be the rotation-gauge field $\Omega$ of the gravitational field on flat spacetime (Definition \claimref{obj.synthesis.gtg-flat-spacetime-gauge-fields}), written as Lorentz-connection one-forms in an orthonormal physical frame, $R^{ab} = d\omega^{ab} + \omega^{a}{}_{e}\wedge\omega^{eb}$ its field strength in that frame, and let $Q(\omega) := \epsilon_{abcd}\bigl(\omega^{ab}\wedge d\omega^{cd} + \tfrac23\,\omega^{ab}\wedge\omega^{c}{}_{e}\wedge\omega^{ed}\bigr)$ be its Chern-Simons three-form for the invariant $\epsilon_{abcd}$. Then:
\begin{enumerate}
\item[(i)] $dQ = \epsilon_{abcd}R^{ab}\wedge R^{cd}$ identically: the topological term of Theorem \claimref{dark-energy.frozen-point-makes-stelle-west-vector}(2) is exact, with $Q$ as primitive.
\item[(ii)] On a Kasner approach the restriction of $Q$ to the slice $\Sigma_\varepsilon = \{\tau = \varepsilon\}$ is
\[
Q\big|_{\Sigma_\varepsilon} \;=\; 8\,p_1p_2p_3\;\varepsilon^{-2}\, d^3x ,
\]
so that the divergent part of the curvature-squared action on $\{\tau > \varepsilon\}$ is $-\tfrac{3}{\Lambda}\int_{\Sigma_\varepsilon}Q = -\tfrac{24}{\Lambda}\,p_1p_2p_3\,\varepsilon^{-2}\,\mathrm{Vol}_3$, exactly the integral of Proposition \claimref{dark-energy.frozen-point-datum-kasner-wall}(iii).
\item[(iii)] The functional $S_{\mathrm{ren}} := S + \tfrac{3}{\Lambda}\int_{\Sigma_\varepsilon}Q(\omega)$, the action with the Chern-Simons form of the connection restricted to the wall added on the wall, has the same interior field equations as $S$ (a boundary term changes the boundary conditions of the variational problem, not the Euler-Lagrange equations), is finite as $\varepsilon \to 0$ on the Kasner approach, and its limit is the Einstein-Cartan and cosmological contributions together with the value of $Q$ on the far boundary. The counterterm is local, but it is not intrinsic to the wall: on the Kasner approach the whole surviving value comes from the cubic term in the boost block $\omega^{i0}$, the extrinsic curvature of the slice, the quadratic term vanishing because every nonzero $\omega^{ab}$ carries the index $0$ and $\epsilon_{abcd}$ needs four distinct indices. And $Q$ is a Chern-Simons form, not gauge invariant: under a rotation-gauge transformation (a local Lorentz rotation of the frame) on the slice it shifts by an exact form and a Wess-Zumino term, so the counterterm is defined relative to a frame, here the exceptional frame of Fact \claimref{dark-energy.imported-weighted-limit-schwarzschild-singularity-matching}. The residual ambiguity of the renormalisation is that frame choice together with the $O(\Lambda)$ constant by which the finite part shifts under the corrections of Proposition \claimref{dark-energy.cosmological-constant-does-not-change-residue}.
\end{enumerate}
On the Kasner approach the counterterm's coefficient $8p_1p_2p_3$ is the third elementary symmetric function of the residue, the one Kasner invariant beyond the two relations.
proof: Here $\omega^{ab}$ and $R^{ab}$ are the rotation-gauge field $\Omega$ and its field strength written as forms in an orthonormal physical frame (Fact \claimref{synthesis.imported-gtg-dictionary}(ii) and (iv)), so every step is a computation in Gauge Theory Gravity on one flat chart. (i) is the transgression formula for a quadratic invariant polynomial, here $\epsilon_{abcd}$ on $\mathfrak{so}(1,3)$: $d(\omega\,d\omega) = d\omega\wedge d\omega$ and $d(\omega^3) = 3\,d\omega\wedge\omega^2$ under the invariant pairing, so $dQ = \epsilon(d\omega + \omega^2, d\omega + \omega^2)$ up to the term $\epsilon(\omega^2,\omega^2)$, which vanishes by the invariance of $\epsilon_{abcd}$ under the adjoint action (the Jacobi identity). The script confirms $dQ = \epsilon_{abcd}R^{ab}\wedge R^{cd}$ as an exact identity of forms on the Kasner connection. (ii) On the slice only the terms of $Q$ without a $d\tau$ leg survive. The quadratic term vanishes on the slice for two reasons, either sufficient: every $d\omega^{cd}$ carries a $d\tau$ leg (the connection depends on $\tau$ only and has tangential legs), and every nonzero $\omega^{ab}$ carries the index $0$ while $\epsilon_{abcd}$ needs four distinct indices; and the cubic term reduces to $\tfrac23\epsilon_{i0jk}\,\omega^{i0}\wedge\omega^{j}{}_{0}\wedge\omega^{0k}$ and its index rearrangements: with $\omega^{i0} = (p_i/\tau)e^i$ each is a multiple of $p_1p_2p_3\tau^{-3}e^1\wedge e^2\wedge e^3 = p_1p_2p_3\tau^{-2}d^3x$, and collecting the signs and multiplicities gives the coefficient $8$; the script computes the $(x,y,z)$ component of $Q$ exactly and finds $8p_1p_2p_3\tau^{-2}$. Then $\int_{\tau>\varepsilon}\epsilon RR = \int Q\big|_{\text{far}} - \int_{\Sigma_\varepsilon}Q$ by Stokes, and $-\tfrac3\Lambda\cdot 8p_1p_2p_3\varepsilon^{-2}$ integrates $-\tfrac{3}{\Lambda}\cdot 16 p_1p_2p_3\int_\varepsilon\tau^{-3}d\tau$, matching Proposition \claimref{dark-energy.frozen-point-datum-kasner-wall}(iii). (iii) A boundary term does not change the Euler-Lagrange equations in the interior. By (ii) the added term cancels the wall boundary contribution of the exact topological term identically on the Kasner approach, leaving the far-boundary value of $Q$ and the two remaining terms of the expansion in \claimref{dark-energy.frozen-point-makes-stelle-west-vector}(2), the Einstein-Cartan term ($2\int\epsilon_{abcd}e^ae^bR^{cd}$, whose density is $-8\Lambda\tau$ on the Einstein region) and the cosmological term ($\tfrac{\Lambda}{3}\int\epsilon_{abcd}e^ae^be^ce^d$, whose density is $24\tau$ before the prefactor), all finite as $\varepsilon\to 0$. With the corrections of Proposition \claimref{dark-energy.cosmological-constant-does-not-change-residue}, $\omega^{i0} = (p_i/\tau + \tfrac{\Lambda}{2}(1-p_i)\tau + \dots)e^i$ and the cubic term of $Q$ on the slice acquires, beyond $8p_1p_2p_3\tau^{-2}$, a term of order $\Lambda\tau^0$ and higher: a finite constant, which is the only freedom in the subtraction.

title: Variable exponents: the residue is pointwise, the corrections are subleading
text:
Let $(\hb, \Omega)$ be a gravitational field on flat spacetime (Definition \claimref{obj.synthesis.gtg-flat-spacetime-gauge-fields}) whose derived metric is $g = d\tau^2 - \sum_i\tau^{2p_i(x)}(dx^i)^2$, with smooth exponents $p_i(x)$ taking values in the open Kasner circle ($\sum p_i = 1 = \sum p_i^2$, all $p_i < 1$), and let $e^0 = d\tau$, $e^i = \tau^{p_i(x)}dx^i$ be the orthonormal coframe of $g$. Then the rotation-gauge field $\Omega$, written as the connection one-forms of $g$ in this coframe (its Levi-Civita connection), is
\[
\omega^{i0} \;=\; \frac{p_i(x)}{\tau}\,e^i, \qquad
\omega^{ij} \;=\; \log\tau\;\Bigl[(\partial_i p_j)\,\tau^{-p_i}\,e^j \;-\; (\partial_j p_i)\,\tau^{-p_j}\,e^i\Bigr] ,
\]
so the boost block is the pointwise Kasner pole with no correction, and the tangential block is singular of order $\tau^{-p_{\max}}|\log\tau|$ with $p_{\max} := \max_j p_j < 1$: subleading to the pole. Every term of the field strength $\mathcal{R}(B)$ beyond the Kasner double pole of Proposition \claimref{dark-energy.frozen-point-datum-kasner-wall}(i) is of relative order $\tau^{1-p_{\max}}|\log\tau|^m$, $m \leq 2$, and tends to zero: the leading field equations at the wall are the Kasner relations pointwise in $x$, the residue of the datum's pole is the pointwise Kasner boost, and the wall counterterm of Proposition \claimref{dark-energy.wall-counterterm} has density $8\,p_1p_2p_3(x)\,\varepsilon^{-2}d^3x$ pointwise.
proof: The structure equations below are those of the derived metric of the gravitational field; by Fact \claimref{synthesis.imported-gtg-dictionary}(ii) their unique torsion-free solution is the rotation-gauge field $\Omega$ written in the coframe. $de^i = p_i\tau^{p_i-1}d\tau\wedge dx^i + \sum_j(\partial_jp_i)\log\tau\,\tau^{p_i}dx^j\wedge dx^i = (p_i/\tau)\,e^0\wedge e^i + \sum_j(\partial_jp_i)\log\tau\,\tau^{-p_j}\,e^j\wedge e^i$. The displayed $\omega$ is antisymmetric, and $de^i + \omega^{i}{}_{0}\wedge e^0 + \omega^{i}{}_{j}\wedge e^j = 0$ with $\omega^{i}{}_{j} = \omega^{ik}\eta_{kj} = -\omega^{ij}$: the boost term cancels the $e^0\wedge e^i$ part as in Proposition \claimref{dark-energy.frozen-point-datum-kasner-wall}, and $-\omega^{ij}\wedge e^j = \log\tau\,(\partial_jp_i)\tau^{-p_j}e^i\wedge e^j$ cancels the tangential part $\sum_j(\partial_jp_i)\log\tau\,\tau^{-p_j}e^j\wedge e^i$ of $de^i$ term by term, the $e^j\wedge e^j$ piece vanishing; this is the Levi-Civita connection of the diagonal three-metric $\sum_i a_i^2(dx^i)^2$ on the slice, $\omega^{ij} = (\partial_i a_j/a_i)dx^j - (\partial_j a_i/a_j)dx^i$ with $a_i = \tau^{p_i(x)}$, in the convention $\omega^{i}{}_{j} = -\omega^{ij}$ of \claimref{dark-energy.imported-macdowell-mansouri-theorem-stelle-west}; $de^0 = 0$ and $\omega^{0}{}_{i}\wedge e^i = \sum_i(p_i/\tau)e^i\wedge e^i = 0$. Uniqueness of the torsion-free metric connection makes this the Levi-Civita connection. Orders: the tangential block is $O(\tau^{-p_{\max}}|\log\tau|)$ against $O(\tau^{-1})$ for the boost block, and $p_{\max} < 1$ on the open Kasner circle. In the curvature, $d\omega^{i0}$ acquires the terms $(\partial_jp_i)(1 + p_i\log\tau)\tau^{-1-p_j}e^j\wedge e^i$; $\omega^{i}{}_{j}\wedge\omega^{j0}$ is $O(\tau^{-1-p_j}|\log\tau|)$; $d\omega^{ij}$ is $O(\tau^{-1-p_j}|\log\tau|) + O(\tau^{-p_j-p_k}|\log\tau|)$; and $\omega^{i}{}_{k}\wedge\omega^{kj}$ is $O(\tau^{-p_j-p_k}\log^2\tau)$. Against the Kasner terms of order $\tau^{-2}$, each is of relative order at most $\tau^{1-p_{\max}}|\log\tau|^2$, which tends to zero. Hence the Ricci tensor at order $\tau^{-2}$ is that of Proposition \claimref{dark-energy.frozen-point-datum-kasner-wall}(ii) with $p = p(x)$; the slice value of $Q$ at order $\varepsilon^{-2}$ is that of Proposition \claimref{dark-energy.wall-counterterm}(ii) with $p = p(x)$ by the same order counting (here the quadratic term of $Q$ no longer vanishes identically, since $d\omega^{ij}$ has tangential legs, but it is of lower order in $\tau^{-1}$); and the subleading orders carry the momentum constraints, which are not analysed here. The script confirms the displayed connection as an identity of the exterior algebra: with the structure coefficients $(p_i/\tau)$ and $(\partial_jp_i)\log\tau\,\tau^{-p_j}$ replaced by independent rational placeholders, the torsion of the displayed $\omega$ vanishes identically, and the connection with the opposite tangential sign does not.

title: What the three discharges leave
text: The residue statement of Assembly \claimref{dark-energy.forcing-half-schwarzschild-wall-residue-sense} now holds with $\Lambda$ (Proposition \claimref{dark-energy.cosmological-constant-does-not-change-residue}), with a finite renormalised action whose only ambiguity is a scheme constant (Proposition \claimref{dark-energy.wall-counterterm}), and pointwise for the diagonal variable-exponent class (Lemma \claimref{dark-energy.variable-exponents-residue-pointwise-corrections-are}), where the sheaf paper's variable-order structure \cite[\S 9]{ButlerT4} is the Gram-level counterpart. What is not done: the subleading momentum constraints of the variable-exponent class, which decide which exponent fields $p_i(x)$ the equations admit, and the non-diagonal class, where the frame directions themselves rotate as the wall is approached; both are the dynamical half of the sheaf paper's connection-level matching \cite[Rem.~8.28]{ButlerT4}, and the logarithm in Lemma \claimref{dark-energy.variable-exponents-residue-pointwise-corrections-are} is the first sign of the variable-order structure at connection level.

title: One way to grip: the acoustic no-go
One way to grip: the acoustic no-go
text: If the graviton is a collective mode of the boundary-mode pairs, an acoustic mode of the correlations, then a question of principle precedes any question of engineering: does anything couple to the metric-forming correlations more efficiently than mass-energy does? Within the s-wave-reduced theory that T5 establishes, the answer is provably no, and this section closes every named open item of the argument.

title: Imported: conformal orthogonality, and the Sugawara construction
text: In a two-dimensional conformal field theory: the two-point function of quasi-primary operators of unequal scaling dimension vanishes in the conformal vacuum; and the stress tensor of a current algebra is the Sugawara bilinear of the currents, the dimension-two member of the vacuum family. \emph{Provenance:} textbook \cite[Ch.~4-5 for the two-point functions, Ch.~15 for the Sugawara construction]{DiFrancesco1997}.
