title: The acoustic no-go: one way to grip
text: In the current-algebra description of the boundary modes (Fact \claimref{dark-energy.imported-s-wave-current-algebra}) let $\varphi$ be a state invariant under the $U(1)$ gauge group of the currents, under charge conjugation $C$ ($J \mapsto -J$, $T \mapsto T$), and under the modular flow generated by the zero mode $L_0$ of the Sugawara stress tensor $T$: the conformal vacuum is such a state, and so is the induced state of Fact \claimref{dark-energy.imported-s-wave-current-algebra} under premise (Q), with charge conjugation implemented on the mode array $\psi_k$ (the fermion modes of the singularity paper's array, Fact \claimref{dark-energy.imported-s-wave-current-algebra}) as the particle-hole reflection about the sea level, $C\psi_kC^{-1} = \psi^\dagger_{-k}$, so that $J \mapsto -J$ and $T \mapsto T$; the proof shows that this state has the three invariances, and the proposition is conditional on (Q) wherever it is applied to it. The graviton mode is $T$. Let $O$ be a probe that is gauge-charged (a fermion field, a condensate order parameter, any operator of nonzero $U(1)$ charge) or neutral and $C$-odd (the charge and spin currents), or, more generally, that lies in a nontrivial irreducible representation of any symmetry of the algebra that $\varphi$ respects and $T$ is invariant under. Then the linear susceptibility of the graviton mode to $O$ vanishes identically: $\varphi(T\,O) = 0$, and likewise for every mode $T_n$. At first order, nothing couples to the pair correlations except the $C$-even neutral subalgebra; in the conformal vacuum that subalgebra's overlap with $T$ is carried by $T$ alone, while in the thermal state it is the whole $C$-even neutral subalgebra, generated by the current bilinears and strictly larger than the conformal family of $T$, that can couple. In the conformal vacuum the statement is strengthened by Fact \claimref{dark-energy.imported-conformal-orthogonality-sugawara-construction}: every quasi-primary of dimension other than two is orthogonal to $T$ as well, so the only quasi-primary with nonzero overlap is $T$. The equivalence principle thereby acquires its converse at this level: fields differ in how strongly they couple, and the reduced theory proves there is no other channel through which to couple. \emph{Level:} the orthogonality is proved below for any state with the stated invariances; that the induced state of Fact \claimref{dark-energy.imported-s-wave-current-algebra} has them is proved in the proof from premise (Q), and is conditional on (Q); that the thermal $C$-even neutral subalgebra is strictly larger than the conformal family of $T$ is a remark, not used.
proof:
The induced state under (Q): a gauge-invariant quasi-free state is $U(1)$-invariant by definition and invariant under the flow it is KMS for; and since a quasi-free state is determined by its two-point function, and $C$ carries $\langle\psi^\dagger_k\psi_kangle = n_k$ to $\langle\psi_{-k}\psi^\dagger_{-k}angle = 1 - n_{-k}$, it is $C$-invariant exactly when $n_{-k} = 1 - n_k$, which the Fermi-Dirac occupancies $n_k = (1 + e^{ eta\kappa k})^{-1}$ of (Q), with $\omega_{-k} = -\omega_k$ about the sea level $k = 0$, satisfy identically. One invariance per case. Charged: for the gauge rotation $\alpha_\vartheta$ and a probe of charge $q 
eq 0$, invariance of $\varphi$ and neutrality of $T$ give $\varphi(T O) = \varphi(\alpha_\vartheta(T O)) = e^{iq\vartheta}\,\varphi(T O)$ for all $\vartheta$, hence $\varphi(TO) = 0$. $C$-odd: $\varphi(T O) = \varphi(C(T O)) = \varphi(T\cdot(-O)) = -\varphi(TO)$, hence zero. The general case is the same argument with the symmetry's characters. In the conformal vacuum, Fact \claimref{dark-energy.imported-conformal-orthogonality-sugawara-construction} adds the orthogonality of quasi-primaries of unequal dimension, which makes the overlap with every probe of dimension other than two vanish whatever its charges; the two arguments together leave $T$ as the unique quasi-primary with nonzero overlap. In the thermal state the dimension argument is not available: $\varphi_ eta(T) 
eq 0$ is already a nonvanishing pairing between dimensions two and zero, and for a charged ensemble ($\varphi(J_0) 
eq 0$, which breaks $C$) the energy-charge covariance $\varphi(L_0 J_0) - \varphi(L_0)\varphi(J_0)$ is a nonzero thermodynamic derivative. This is why the hypothesis is the symmetry of the state and not the vanishing of two-point functions by dimension, and why the $C$-symmetric charge-zero sector is named. What remains after the symmetries are used is the $C$-even neutral part of the algebra, which for the $u(1)$ current algebra of Fact \claimref{dark-energy.imported-s-wave-current-algebra} is generated as an algebra by the normal-ordered bilinears of the currents; $T$ belongs to it, and so do the quartic and higher $C$-even neutral products, which in the thermal state, where the dimension argument is unavailable, can overlap $T$. The script exhibits the mechanism on a six-mode window with exact rational occupancies: the energy-charge covariance vanishes exactly in a charge-conjugation-symmetric state and is exactly nonzero at nonzero chemical potential, and the overlap of the flow generator with every off-diagonal (nonzero-weight) probe vanishes exactly.

title: Weakness as dimension; the nonlinear bound; the open items named
text: Four consequences, each at its level. \emph{Structural:} coupling to a dimension-two operator is irrelevant, suppressed at energy $E$ by $(E/\Lambda_{\mathrm{cut}})^2$ relative to dimension-one couplings, which is exactly the form $GE^2$ with the cutoff at the Planck scale: weakness is a consequence of compositeness, the collective mode being one dimension above the currents. This supplies the weakness's functional form, not its number; the smallness problem stands. \emph{Consistency:} the first nonvanishing vertex is cubic, $\langle TJJ\rangle \neq 0$, two currents fusing to the stress tensor: translated out of boundary-mode language this is the Gertsenshtein process \cite{Gertsenshtein1962}, already present in classical general relativity with its known and unobservably small efficiency; that the current algebra reproduces the correct leading vertex is a check passed, and that it produces nothing stronger is the conclusion on engineering. \emph{The coherence loophole, closed by the hypothesis:} a background with $\langle J\rangle \neq 0$ breaks the charge-conjugation symmetry that Proposition \claimref{dark-energy.acoustic-no-go-one-way-grip} assumes, linearises the quadratic, and seems to offer a first-order channel; but the cross term is precisely the background's own stress-energy, which is what the broken symmetry admits: enhancement by coherence is general relativity's own gravitomagnetism, not a new coupling, and by reciprocity the same orthogonality that forbids a source forbids an enhanced detector. \emph{The open items, named so the no-go can be tested where they stand:} (i) the proposition is stated in the s-wave reduction, and the four-dimensional lift's inheritance must be established, not asserted; (ii) if the second variation of Theorem \claimref{dark-energy.frozen-point-makes-stelle-west-vector}'s functional carries a component along fluctuations of $I$ itself, the argument must extend to that sector. Proposition \claimref{dark-energy.point-infinity-has-no-physical-fluctuation} closes (ii); Assembly \claimref{dark-energy.lift-inherits-no-go-steps-itemised} addresses (i) at its level.

title: The point at infinity has no physical fluctuation: the $(I,V)$-sector is pure gauge
text:
Take the functional in its three-argument form, $S[
abla, I, V] \sim Q(I)^{-1}\int\epsilon(I, V, F, F)$, with $
abla$ the tractor connection, on flat spacetime the $\Cl(2,4)$ gauge field $\Omega_{T}$ of Theorem \claimref{synthesis.gtg-tractor-gauge-field-reproduces-tractor-connection} (its curvature $F$ the field strength of $\Omega_{T}$), and $I$ and $V$ independent sections subject to the Stelle-West constraints $Q(I) = \Lambda/3$, $\ip{V}{I} = 0$, $Q(V) = -3/\Lambda$; Lemma \claimref{dark-energy.stelle-west-vector-frozen-point} exhibits $V = X - (3/\Lambda)I$ as the canonical solution of the constraints on the Einstein region, but inside the variational principle $V$ is a field, since the canonical tractor $X$ is a fixed section and a transformation acting on $
abla$ and $I$ alone is not a symmetry of a functional that contains $X$. Then: the constrained fluctuation space of $(I, V)$ has dimension $9$ (twelve components less three independent linearised constraints; it fibres over the five tangential directions of $I$ with four-dimensional affine fibres of $\delta V$, and is not a direct sum); the stabiliser of the pair $(I, V)$ in $SO(2,4)$ is the Lorentz group of $\{I,V\}^\perp$, of dimension six, so the broken generators number $15 - 6 = 9$; and the infinitesimal action $\xi \mapsto (\xi\cdot I, \xi\cdot V)$ of the broken generators onto the constrained fluctuation space is bijective. Unitary gauge $\delta I = \delta V = 0$ therefore exists and is complete: every fluctuation of the pair is a gauge transformation, the eaten Goldstone modes reappearing as the frame freedom of the soldering form (the physical frame $\hb^{-1}(a)$ of the gravitational field, up to rotation gauge), the Stelle-West mechanism read in reverse. In unitary gauge the second variation of the action has legs only on the connection: the graviton carries no $(\delta I, \delta V)$ polarisation. This closes open item (ii) of Remark \claimref{note.dark-energy.weakness-dimension-nonlinear-bound-open-items} within the action's own variational principle; the four-dimensional lift of the s-wave no-go is the task of Assembly \claimref{dark-energy.lift-inherits-no-go-steps-itemised}, not of this proposition. \emph{Level:} the counting, the bijectivity, and the invariance of the integrand $\epsilon(I,V,F,F)$ under the ambient group acting on all three arguments are proved outright below; that the functional so gauge-fixed is the MacDowell-Mansouri functional is Theorem \claimref{dark-energy.frozen-point-makes-stelle-west-vector}(ii)-(iii), with its assembly-level clause.
proof:
Read in Gauge Theory Gravity: the metric $g$ below is the derived metric of the gravitational field $(\hb, \Omega)$ on flat spacetime, the manifold is the invertible region, and the tractor connection is the flat-space $\Cl(2,4)$ gauge field of Theorem \claimref{synthesis.gtg-tractor-gauge-field-reproduces-tractor-connection}; the index computation below is its reading in the splitting of $g$ (Fact \claimref{synthesis.imported-gtg-dictionary}).

Constraints: $\delta Q(I) = 2\ip{\delta I}{I} = 0$, $\delta\ip{V}{I} = \ip{\delta V}{I} + \ip{V}{\delta I} = 0$, $\delta Q(V) = 2\ip{\delta V}{V} = 0$: three independent linear conditions on the twelve components of $(\delta I, \delta V)$ (independent because $I$ and $V$ are non-null and orthogonal), leaving nine. Stabiliser: a bivector annihilating both $I$ and $V$ is a bivector of $\{I,V\}^\perp$, which has signature $(1,3)$ (Theorem \claimref{dark-energy.frozen-point-makes-stelle-west-vector}(ii)), so the stabiliser algebra is $\mathfrak{so}(1,3)$, of dimension six, and the broken complement has dimension nine. The map $\xi \mapsto (\xi\cdot I, \xi\cdot V)$ maps into the constrained space, since $\ip{\xi\cdot I}{I} = 0$, $\ip{\xi\cdot V}{V} = 0$ and $\ip{\xi\cdot V}{I} + \ip{V}{\xi\cdot I} = 0$ by antisymmetry of $\xi$; restricted to the broken complement it is injective, because a $\xi$ in the complement with $\xi\cdot I = \xi\cdot V = 0$ lies in the stabiliser; by equal dimensions it is bijective. Any constrained $(\delta I, \delta V)$ is thus $(\xi\cdot I, \xi\cdot V)$ for a unique broken $\xi$, and the gauge transformation by $-\xi$, acting simultaneously on $
abla$, $I$ and $V$, removes it while shifting $\delta
abla$: the Goldstone eating. In the resulting gauge the second variation is a quadratic form in $\delta
abla$ alone. Invariance of the functional: a gauge transformation is a section $g$ of the ambient group bundle, acting on the fibre by $g(x) \in SO(2,4)$ at each point; it acts on the connection by $
abla \mapsto g
abla g^{-1}$, so that the curvature, $F = 
abla^2$, transforms by $F \mapsto gFg^{-1}$, that is, its bivector value at each point is carried by $g(x)$ (a bivector $a\wedge b$ goes to $ga\wedge gb$, since $g$ is an isometry), and on $I$ and $V$ by $I \mapsto gI$, $V \mapsto gV$. The volume form of a six-dimensional fibre with a nondegenerate form is invariant under its special orthogonal group, so at each point $\epsilon(gI, gV, gF, gF) = \det(g)\,\epsilon(I, V, F, F) = \epsilon(I, V, F, F)$; the prefactor $1/Q(I)$ and the three constraints $Q(I) = \Lambda/3$, $\ip{V}{I} = 0$, $Q(V) = -3/\Lambda$ are preserved because $g(x)$ is an isometry of the fibre; and a pointwise identity between integrands is an identity between the integrals. The functional is therefore invariant, and the constraint surface is carried to itself, under the ambient gauge group acting on all three arguments. The script confirms the fibrewise identity on rational elements of $SO(2,4)$ (a boost, a rotation, and their product, each confirmed an isometry). That the one-argument version fails is worth recording, since it is the error to avoid: with $\xi = I\wedge V$ one has $\xi\cdot I = -(\Lambda/3)V$, a tangential fluctuation of $I$, but $\xi\cdot X = -(3/\Lambda)I - V$, so that $\epsilon(I, \xi\cdot X, F, F) = -\epsilon(I, V, F, F)$: acting on $
abla$ and $I$ while holding $X$ fixed changes the integrand by minus itself, not by zero. The script performs the counting exactly in the flat model over $\mathbb{Q}$ at $\Lambda = 3$: the joint action matrix of the fifteen basis bivectors on $(I, V)$ has rank exactly nine, so the stabiliser has dimension six; the image of the bivector algebra on $I$ alone has rank five and equals $I^\perp$; and the one-argument failure is confirmed on the displayed $\xi$.

title: The lift inherits the no-go, with its steps itemised
text:
The remaining open item, that the four-dimensional lift might introduce a coupling invisible to the s-wave sector, is addressed by covering the spacetime in two pieces, with one step upgraded. The steps, each with its provenance:
\begin{enumerate}
\item \emph{Partial waves (exact, kinematic).} Near the horizon the four-dimensional two-point function between the graviton mode and any probe decomposes over partial waves, and the angular integration is diagonal in $\ell$ by spherical-harmonic orthogonality.
\item \emph{Near-horizon reduction (assembly, at the level it carries in T5).} Each fixed-$\ell$ sector reduces, at the horizon where the potential barrier vanishes, to a two-dimensional copy of the setting of the current algebra, in which the $\ell$-th component of the graviton mode is the $\ell$-th $\mathfrak{su}(2)$-harmonic of the current bilinears. Which operator is the stress tensor in the $\ell$-th copy is fixed by step (4), not assumed.
\item \emph{Exterior exactness (imported theorem).} On any region where the gauge-theoretic metric is invertible, the horizon included, the description coincides exactly with classical general relativity, by the geometry paper's import of gauge-theory gravity from Lasenby, Doran and Gull \cite[Fact~2.1]{ButlerT6}, whose couplings to the metric are stress-energy alone. The two pieces overlap and cover the spacetime.
\item \emph{The sphere step (conditional on the entropy paper's Indifference premise; then proved by covariance).} By the sphere theorem (Fact \claimref{dark-energy.imported-walls-sphere-theorem}, \cite[Thm.~5.5]{ButlerT8}, conditional on \cite[Principle~5.4]{ButlerT8}) every angular operator of the lift is a boundary-mode bilinear of definite spin under the adjoint $\mathfrak{su}(2)$, of spin $\ell \geq 1$ for every non-trivial harmonic, while the s-wave stress tensor $T$ is an $\mathfrak{su}(2)$ singlet. In an $\mathfrak{su}(2)$-invariant state the symmetry orthogonality of Proposition \claimref{dark-energy.acoustic-no-go-one-way-grip} applies verbatim: nonzero spin, zero overlap. Orthogonality by dimension would \emph{not} do here, the bilinears having dimension two like $T$; it is the spin that separates them. The lift inherits the no-go because the sphere is built from the same correlations to which the no-go applies, and those correlations carry spin.
\end{enumerate}
With Propositions \claimref{dark-energy.acoustic-no-go-one-way-grip} and \claimref{dark-energy.point-infinity-has-no-physical-fluctuation} and these steps, the acoustic programme is closed at the mixed level of its inputs: the metric-forming correlations admit exactly one coupling sector, its weakness is dimensional, its leading nonlinearity is Gertsenshtein's, and its Goldstones are eaten. Step (2), the near-horizon reduction, is at assembly level, its promotion shared with T5 and T7; step (4) is conditional on the entropy paper's Indifference premise, and the closure of the acoustic programme inherits that condition.
proof: Follows from \claimref{dark-energy.acoustic-no-go-one-way-grip}, \claimref{dark-energy.point-infinity-has-no-physical-fluctuation}, \claimref{dark-energy.imported-walls-sphere-theorem}, \claimref{scrambling.principality-indifference-sphere}, \claimref{scrambling.indifference-structural-premise-series} and \claimref{interior.imported-equivalence-einstein-equations}, as the source states.

title: What kind of number the norm is: the fourth alternative
text: Proposition \claimref{dark-energy.point-infinity-has-no-physical-fluctuation} treats $\Lambda$ as a number fixed before variation, the value of the Stelle-West constraints. The Standard-Model paper \cite[Prop.~7.6]{ButlerT12} classifies the same number, in the form $N = M_P/H$ with $H^2 = Q(I) = \Lambda/3$ on the de Sitter region (Fact \claimref{dark-energy.imported-frozen-point-geometry} for the norm, Theorem \claimref{dark-energy.frozen-point-makes-stelle-west-vector} for its identification with the Stelle-West value), in four clauses. Clause (1) proves that $N$ is not kinematic: under $\Lambda \to s^2\Lambda$ at fixed $M_P$, that is $I \to sI$ with the conformal class unchanged, $N \to N/s$ while every discrete invariant that paper derives is unchanged, so $N$ does not factor through the kinematic isomorphism class (Fact \claimref{standard-model.trichotomy-what-kind-number} below). Clause (2) imports from this paper that it is not dynamical, the norm being fixed by a constraint and not evolved: its \cite[Fact~2.10]{ButlerT12} cites Proposition \claimref{dark-energy.point-infinity-has-no-physical-fluctuation} and Proposition \claimref{dark-energy.vacuum-region-registration-condition}(i). Clause (3) concludes that $N$ is initial data carried by the boundary at the origin, conditionally on three things: on the three alternatives kinematic, dynamical, initial data being exhaustive, on the dating observation \cite[Obs.~7.4]{ButlerT12} that locates the boundary, and on the promotion decision its clause (4) names. Clause (4) imports from this subsection what follows. This subsection records, at the level of the action that belongs to this paper, that the three alternatives are not exhaustive, that the missing alternative is exactly where the action as written puts $N$, and what modification of the action would move it.

title: Four ways a number enters a theory of this shape
The four alternatives are exhaustive; the three are not
text: Every conserved $q$ is (D), (P) or (I), and exactly one of them; (K) can hold together with any of them and is excluded by none; (D) implies (K), while (P) and (I) are compatible with (K) and with its negation. A conserved $q$ that is neither (K), (D) nor (I) is (P). Hence the inference ``not kinematic, not dynamical, therefore initial data'' is valid only if (P) is excluded.
proof: Either $q$ is constant on every $\mathcal{S}_\mu$ or it is not. If not, it is (I). If so, either its common value is the same for all $\mu$, which is (D), or it is not, which is (P). The three cases are disjoint by construction and cover every $q$; (K) is a statement about factoring through $\mathcal{K}$, which none of the three excludes; (D) implies it, since a constant factors through every kinematic class, while (P) and (I) are compatible with (K) and with its negation (a kinematic invariant can be constant, parameter-dependent, or vary within a solution space, according to how $\mathcal{K}$ is embedded in the configuration space). The last sentence is the contrapositive of the disjunction.

title: Under the action as written, the norm is a parameter of the laws
proof: (i) is Proposition \claimref{dark-energy.point-infinity-has-no-physical-fluctuation}'s count read as a statement about the norm: the three linearised constraints are independent because $I$ and $V$ are non-null and orthogonal, the constrained space is $12 - 3 = 9$, and every constrained fluctuation is a gauge transformation, so the norm cannot fluctuate; that $H^2 = Q(I) = \Lambda/3$ on the de Sitter region is Fact \claimref{dark-energy.imported-frozen-point-geometry}'s norm with Theorem \claimref{dark-energy.frozen-point-makes-stelle-west-vector}'s identification of it as the Stelle-West value. (ii): the script verifies $d(N^2)/d\Lambda = -3M_P^2/\Lambda^2$ as an identity of rational functions in $\Lambda$ and evaluates $N^2$ at two rational values of $\Lambda$ to unequal values; the rescaling clause is Fact \claimref{standard-model.trichotomy-what-kind-number}: $\Lambda \to s^2\Lambda$ with the conformal class unchanged changes $N$ and not the kinematic isomorphism class, so $N$ does not factor through that class. (iii) is Proposition \claimref{dark-energy.four-alternatives-are-exhaustive-three-are}. The free case: the linearised constraints acquire the columns $-\tfrac13\,\delta\Lambda$ and $-(3/\Lambda^2)\,\delta\Lambda$ in the first and third rows; the script, at the same rational instance Proposition \claimref{dark-energy.point-infinity-has-no-physical-fluctuation}'s checks use, computes rank three on thirteen variables, rank nine of the fifteen gauge images extended by a zero $\delta\Lambda$-component, rank ten of those images together with the displayed norm mode (so the mode is not a gauge direction and spans the complement), and checks that the norm mode satisfies the free constraints, violates the fixed ones, and equals $1/(2\Lambda)$ times the $s$-derivative of $(sI, V/s, s^2\Lambda)$ at $s = 1$, the derivative taken componentwise on the family as a vector of rational functions in a formal $s$, whose members satisfy the constraints at $s^2\Lambda$ as identities in $s$.

title: What clause (3) requires, and what it yields: the promotion is a decision
text: The Standard-Model paper's dating observation reads $N$ as fixed at the origin and constant since, which is the (I) reading: a constant of integration. Proposition \claimref{dark-energy.under-action-written-norm-parameter-laws} says the action as written does not deliver that reading; it delivers (P). The two are reconciled by a known class of modifications of the action (Henneaux-Teitelboim \cite{HenneauxTeitelboim1989}; Brown-Teitelboim \cite{BrownTeitelboim1988}; Kaloper-Padilla sequestering \cite{KaloperPadilla2014}), of which the Henneaux-Teitelboim promotion is the one used here (Fact \claimref{dark-energy.imported-henneaux-teitelboim-promotion}): promote the Stelle-West norm from a fixed number to the value of a Lagrange-multiplier field whose constancy is an equation of motion, so that the norm mode of Proposition \claimref{dark-energy.under-action-written-norm-parameter-laws} acquires the equation $d\Lambda = 0$ and $\Lambda$ becomes a label of the solution rather than of the theory. This is a modification of the action, carrying a conjugate cosmic-time variable with it, and it is a decision for the series, not a theorem of this paper; it is recorded as open, with both branches stated, and the Standard-Model paper's classification is to be read with its clause (3) resting on it. Two things follow whichever way the decision goes. First, the entropic and null-endpoint forces that the classification's discussion names act on a measure over $\Lambda$, and a measure over the values of a parameter of the laws is a measure over theories, while a measure over initial data is a measure within one theory; the descent measure the series does not possess is one or the other, and which one is the decision just named. Second, the rescaling $\Lambda \to s^2\Lambda$ maps $\mathcal{S}_\Lambda$ to $\mathcal{S}_{s^2\Lambda}$ isomorphically: under (P) it is an isomorphism between different theories, under (I) a symmetry of one theory's solution space, and only in the second case is ``why this $\Lambda$'' a question the theory can be asked to answer. If the promotion is adopted, the Goldstone count of Proposition \claimref{dark-energy.point-infinity-has-no-physical-fluctuation} is to be recomputed with the norm mode and its conjugate time as dynamical variables, a ten-dimensional constrained space with one physical direction; if it is rejected, the count stands and the dating observation is withdrawn from initial-data status. Successor problem (5) reads: the smallness of $\Lambda$ cannot be addressed until this decision is made, and then until the measure is available.

title: Imported: the Henneaux-Teitelboim promotion
text: In the unimodular formulation of general relativity the cosmological constant is not a parameter of the action but the value of a Lagrange-multiplier field, conjugate to a cosmic-time variable, whose constancy $d\Lambda = 0$ is an equation of motion; $\Lambda$ is then a constant of integration, a label of the solution rather than of the theory, and the formulation is generally covariant. \emph{Provenance:} \cite{HenneauxTeitelboim1989}; the transcription to the Stelle-West norm, promoting the value $\Lambda/3$ of the constraint $Q(I) = \Lambda/3$ to that field, is Remark \claimref{note.dark-energy.what-clause-3-requires-what-it}'s, and is the decision that remark leaves open.
provenance: M. Henneaux and C. Teitelboim, The cosmological constant and general covariance, Phys. Lett. B 222 (1989), 195--199.

title: The engineering conclusion, and scope
The conclusion does not depend on the ontology, at its level
text: The gravitational-engineering conclusion, that the metric-forming structure admits exactly one coupling sector (stress-energy), with no selective coupling, no enhanced source and no enhanced detector at first order, holds on either reading of the graviton's ontology, with a different level on each. If the graviton is the framework's collective mode: by derivation, Propositions \claimref{dark-energy.acoustic-no-go-one-way-grip} and \claimref{dark-energy.point-infinity-has-no-physical-fluctuation} at proof level within the s-wave sector and Assembly \claimref{dark-energy.lift-inherits-no-go-steps-itemised} for the lift. If the graviton is fundamental: by Weinberg's soft theorem \cite{Weinberg1964}, the leading low-energy coupling of any massless spin-two particle is universal, which is the equivalence principle and rules out a selective coupling at leading order; non-minimal couplings, subleading in energy, are not excluded by the theorem, so the fundamental branch delivers the conclusion at leading order only. The conclusion is therefore common ground between the ontologies at leading order; what is distinctive to the composite reading is the ultraviolet behaviour (quantisation as output; no graviton loops to renormalise), the derivation of weakness as dimensional suppression (Remark \claimref{note.dark-energy.weakness-dimension-nonlinear-bound-open-items}), and the $\ell_P^2/A$ corrections carried by the spectrum paper; the discriminating experiments, if any, lie in those corrections, and the asymmetry (hard to refute, hard to confirm below the Planck scale) is stated rather than hidden. The steps: the composite branch is the cited chain with its declared levels; the fundamental branch is the imported theorem read within its scope; the structural consequence recorded is that were the composite reading wrong, the leading-order conclusion would survive it.
proof: Follows from \claimref{dark-energy.acoustic-no-go-one-way-grip}, \claimref{dark-energy.point-infinity-has-no-physical-fluctuation} and \claimref{dark-energy.lift-inherits-no-go-steps-itemised}, as the source states.

title: Successor problems
text: Five, the first two the most precisely posed. (1) \emph{The forcing half beyond the diagonal class:} Assembly \claimref{dark-energy.forcing-half-schwarzschild-wall-residue-sense} with Propositions \claimref{dark-energy.cosmological-constant-does-not-change-residue}-\claimref{dark-energy.wall-counterterm} and Lemma \claimref{dark-energy.variable-exponents-residue-pointwise-corrections-are} answers it in the residue sense for the diagonal Kasner class with $\Lambda$ and variable exponents. Analyse the subleading momentum constraints, which select the admissible exponent fields $p_i(x)$, and the non-diagonal class, where the frame rotates as the wall is approached; this is the dynamical half of the sheaf paper's connection-level matching, and the logarithm of Lemma \claimref{dark-energy.variable-exponents-residue-pointwise-corrections-are} is where the variable-order structure enters. (2) \emph{The dual wall:} Theorem \claimref{dark-energy.walls-free-sector}'s symmetric form $M$ belongs to walls of the soldering form, metrics on tangent vectors with a radical. Decide whether such walls occur in the series' geometries (the unweighted sphere directions of the Schwarzschild interior are of this type before the sheaf paper's weights absorb them) and, where they do, whether $M$ carries a boundary mode space; the gauge generator the sheaf paper's wall opens, the ladder boost of Proposition \claimref{dark-energy.sheaf-papers-wall-soldering-variables}(iii), is the object to compare it with. (3) \emph{Matter coupling at $\Sigma$, and the frozen point off the vacuum region:} extend the polynomial functional by matter in a form that remains defined across the locus, determine what the wall does to minimal coupling, and define the frozen point on a matter-filled region in a way that keeps it parallel, which Proposition \claimref{dark-energy.vacuum-region-registration-condition}(iii) needs and Proposition \claimref{dark-energy.vacuum-region-registration-condition}(ii) shows the naive scale tractor does not supply. (4) \emph{The Kerr version of the no-go:} the ring's codimension-two exceptional structure replaces the wall; the orthogonality argument needs the rotating current algebra, and the duality monodromy of the geometry paper will enter. (5) \emph{The smallness of $\Lambda$, and the promotion decision:} Theorem \claimref{dark-energy.frozen-point-makes-stelle-west-vector}(2) gives the form of the action for $\Lambda \neq 0$, not a value and not smallness, and the numerical layer is the declared open problem of the matter papers. Proposition \claimref{dark-energy.under-action-written-norm-parameter-laws} places the question exactly: under the action as written $\Lambda$ indexes the theory, and ``why this $\Lambda$'' is a question within one theory only if a modification of the known class of Remark \claimref{note.dark-energy.what-clause-3-requires-what-it}, the Henneaux-Teitelboim promotion being the one used there, is adopted. Decide the promotion; if adopted, recompute the Goldstone count of Proposition \claimref{dark-energy.point-infinity-has-no-physical-fluctuation} with the norm mode and its conjugate time, and name the measure over $\Lambda$ on which the Standard-Model paper's entropic and null-endpoint forces act.

title: Position in the series
Position in the series
text:
This paper is T10 of the series. \emph{It relies on eight papers:} the primer T0 \cite{ButlerT0} for the Clifford and bivector language; the root paper T1 \cite{ButlerT1} for the standard of proof and the Fact (imported) discipline every result here is held to; the sheaf paper T4 \cite{ButlerT4} for the continuation of the ambient structure across a tame wall and the corank-one radical (Fact \claimref{dark-energy.imported-walls-sphere-theorem}); the singularity paper T5 \cite{ButlerT5} for the s-wave current algebra and, under the singularity paper's premise (Q), its thermal state (Fact \claimref{dark-energy.imported-s-wave-current-algebra}); the geometry paper T6 \cite{ButlerT6} for the frozen point, the tractor connection and the exterior exactness (Fact \claimref{dark-energy.imported-frozen-point-geometry}, Assembly \claimref{dark-energy.lift-inherits-no-go-steps-itemised}); the Hawking paper T7 \cite{ButlerT7} for the finite-window quantification of the current algebra; the entropy paper T8 \cite{ButlerT8} for the sphere theorem that carries the sphere step (Fact \claimref{dark-energy.imported-walls-sphere-theorem}); and, later in the series, the standard-model paper T12 \cite{ButlerT12} for the rescaling argument that the norm is not kinematic (Fact \claimref{standard-model.trichotomy-what-kind-number}), with no circularity, since that argument uses only the conformal class and the pair structure.

\emph{Papers that rely on this one:} the mass paper T11 \cite{ButlerT11} imports the action theorem (Theorem \claimref{dark-energy.frozen-point-makes-stelle-west-vector}) for its gravity assembly; the standard-model paper T12 \cite{ButlerT12} shares the two-kinds theorem (Theorem \claimref{dark-energy.gravity-pre-metric-forces-degenerate-exactly}), uses the action's single coupling, and reads its classification's initial-data clause against Proposition \claimref{dark-energy.under-action-written-norm-parameter-laws}; the dark-matter paper T14 \cite{ButlerT14} imports the acoustic no-go and the $w = -1$ registration (Proposition \claimref{dark-energy.vacuum-region-registration-condition}); the entropy paper T8 \cite{ButlerT8} and the Hawking paper T7 \cite{ButlerT7} refer the engineering no-go and the lift's dynamics to this paper; and the capstone T17 \cite{ButlerT17} tabulates this paper's claims at their tiers.

title: Machine verification
Machine verification
text:
The computational identities asserted in this paper are verified in exact arithmetic by the script \texttt{verify\_T10.py} \cite{ButlerVerifyT10}, which imports the series' shared library \texttt{GA.py}: rational matrix algebra over $\mathbb{Q}$, exact rank and congruence-signature routines, and rational functions in a formal variable. No floating point is used anywhere; ninety checks, all passing, organised in five parts keyed to statement tags; the fifth, on Proposition \claimref{dark-energy.under-action-written-norm-parameter-laws}, computes the free-$\Lambda$ constraint count, the norm mode against the gauge images, and its identification with the tangent of the rescaling family, at the rational instance the Goldstone checks use, with $d(N^2)/d\Lambda$ as a rational-function identity. One check confirms that the withdrawn radical-vanishing claim fails, and two negative controls confirm that refuted alternative readings fail (the one-argument functional, the opposite tangential sign); the checks of Theorem \claimref{dark-energy.gravity-pre-metric-forces-degenerate-exactly}(1) are the trace identities its proof uses, algebraic identities rather than tests, and are labelled so in the script.

\emph{Part A: the frozen point and the Stelle-West vector.} The scale-tractor norm $Q(I) = \Lambda/3$ is confirmed as an identity of rational functions in a formal $\Lambda$, with $I = (1, 0, 0, 0, 0, \Lambda/6)$ in the flat model $\mathbb{R}^{2,4}$ carrying the form $\ip{(\sigma,\mu,\rho)}{(\sigma',\mu',\rho')} \;=\; g(\mu,\mu') + \sigma\rho' + \rho\sigma'$ with $g = \eta$; the normalisation $1/Q(I) = 3/\Lambda$ is confirmed to have a simple pole at $\Lambda = 0$ and nowhere else; the norm identity is also confirmed at the rational instance $\Lambda = 3$. For Lemma \claimref{dark-energy.stelle-west-vector-frozen-point}: with $X = (0,0,0,0,0,1)$ and $V = X - (3/\Lambda)I$ as rational-function vectors, $Q(X) = 0$, $\langle X, I\rangle = 1$, $\langle V, I\rangle = 0$ and $Q(V) = -3/\Lambda$ are confirmed as identities; the model connection bivector $e_a\wedge W$ with $W = V/Q(V) = (1,0,0,0,0,-\Lambda/6)$ is confirmed to annihilate $I$, to send $X$ and $V$ to $e_a$, and to agree with the display \claimref{dark-energy.imported-frozen-point-geometry} on every basis tractor; the bracket $[e_a\wedge W, e_b\wedge W] = (\Lambda/3)\,e_a\wedge e_b$ is confirmed as a matrix identity in formal $\Lambda$; and the slot count of Theorem \claimref{dark-energy.frozen-point-makes-stelle-west-vector}(iii) is confirmed by computing, at $\Lambda = 3$ and for generic integer bivectors, that $\epsilon(I, \cdot, B_1, B_2)$ is a nonzero fibre vector (an integrand with one vector slot open is not a scalar) while $\epsilon(I, V, B_1, B_2) = \epsilon(I, X, B_1, B_2)$ is a scalar. At the rational instance $\Lambda = 3$ the image of all fifteen basis bivectors of $\mathfrak{so}(2,4)$ on $I$ has rank exactly $5$, every image vector is orthogonal to $I$, and $I^{\perp}$ has dimension exactly $5$ with induced form of signature $(1,4)$ by exact congruence, and at $\Lambda = -3$ of signature $(2,3)$, the anti-de Sitter branch; the induced form on $\{I,V\}^\perp$ is confirmed to have signature $(1,3)$ at both values; the first two facts are the stabiliser dimension $10$ and the de Sitter signature of Fact \claimref{dark-energy.imported-frozen-point-geometry}; for Proposition \claimref{dark-energy.point-infinity-has-no-physical-fluctuation} the joint action matrix of the fifteen basis bivectors on the pair $(I, V)$ is confirmed to have rank exactly $9$ (stabiliser of dimension $6$), the constrained fluctuation space to have dimension $9$, the one-argument failure to occur as displayed: $\epsilon(I, \xi\cdot X, B_1, B_2) = -\epsilon(I, V, B_1, B_2) \neq 0$ for $\xi = I\wedge V$; and the invariance $\epsilon(gI, gV, gB_1, gB_2) = \epsilon(I, V, B_1, B_2)$ to hold for three rational elements of $SO(2,4)$ (a boost, a rotation, and their product), each confirmed an isometry on all basis pairs. For the field-space clause of Theorem \claimref{dark-energy.frozen-point-makes-stelle-west-vector}(iii), $[I\wedge u, I\wedge v] = -Q(I)\,u\wedge v$ is confirmed as a matrix identity for $u, v \in I^\perp$ and $\epsilon(I, V, u\wedge v, B_1)$ confirmed nonzero: the $I$-leg components of an unconstrained connection would enter the Lorentz block quadratically.

\emph{Part B: the wall's free sector.} In the normal form $e = \mathrm{diag}(1,1,1,0)$ the connection equation is assembled as an exact $24\times 24$ integer matrix on the torsion components and its rank is confirmed to be $18$, with exactly $3$ identically vanishing rows, and $24$ on the invertible normal form; the frame equation is assembled as a $16\times 36$ matrix on the curvature components and its rank is confirmed to be $16$ in both cases, with no identically vanishing row. The kernel of the wall connection equation is confirmed to consist of torsion components with no $dx^3$ leg and no frame index $3$. At the connection level the equation is assembled as a $24\times 24$ matrix on the components of $\omega$ and its rank confirmed to be $12$, with the kernel confirmed to be exactly the symmetric parts of $K$ and $M$ of Theorem \claimref{dark-energy.walls-free-sector}(b); the principal symbol of the frame equation is assembled in each of the four coordinate directions and its rank on the free sector confirmed to be $0$ on $M$ in every direction, $6$ on $K$ in the radial direction and $3$ on $K$ in each tangential direction; the full quadratic frame equation is evaluated on random elements of the free sector and confirmed to vanish in all components except $E_3(\partial_0,\partial_1,\partial_2)$, where it is confirmed to equal $\sigma_2'(M) - \sigma_2'(K)$ exactly with no cross term, and the cosmological coefficient $-6$ is confirmed. The torsion-level counts, the rank $12$, the symbol ranks and the single surviving component are confirmed for the Riemannian and null normal forms with identical counts (the null form in the frame adapted to its dying direction); the symmetric $K \oplus M$ split, the identity $\sigma_2'(M) - \sigma_2'(K)$ with vanishing cross term and the cosmological coefficient are confirmed for the Riemannian form as well, with the cosmological coefficient $+6$ there, and at the null form the surviving pair $E_0 = -E_1$ is confirmed to carry the cosmological term with coefficient $\pm 6$. The Bianchi-series check also confirms the quoted coefficients $h_{i,1} = (2, \tfrac12, \tfrac12)$ and $h_{i,2} = (-\tfrac{33}{20}, -\tfrac{3}{40}, -\tfrac{3}{40})$ at the Schwarzschild exponents with $\Lambda = 3$. For Proposition \claimref{dark-energy.sheaf-papers-wall-soldering-variables}: the stabiliser algebra of the degenerate internal cometric $\mathrm{diag}(0,\eta_3)$ in $\mathfrak{gl}(4)$ is confirmed to have dimension $7$, with no rotation of the dying direction into the surviving ones and with the dilation present; the ambient form on $(k, m_i, k^*, w)$ is confirmed to have signature $(2,4)$; the subalgebra of $\mathfrak{so}(2,4)$ preserving the degenerate four-plane is confirmed to have dimension $8$ with a restriction of rank $7$; and the lift of the dilation is solved for exactly and confirmed to be $k \mapsto k$, $k^* \mapsto -k^*$ with everything else fixed. For Proposition \claimref{dark-energy.frozen-point-datum-kasner-wall}, with $\tau = s^N$ so that every power is integral: at the two rational Kasner points $(-\tfrac13,\tfrac23,\tfrac23)$ and $(-\tfrac27,\tfrac37,\tfrac67)$ the connection $\omega^{i0} = (p_i/\tau)e^i$ is confirmed torsion-free, its curvature confirmed to be the displayed double pole, the Ricci tensor confirmed to vanish identically, and the Gauss-Bonnet density confirmed to be $-16p_1p_2p_3\tau^{-3}$ ($\tfrac{64}{27}\tau^{-3}$ for Schwarzschild); at the non-Kasner point $(\tfrac15,\tfrac15,\tfrac25)$ the Ricci formulas of (ii) are confirmed as rational-function identities with nonzero value; at the excluded Milne point $(1,0,0)$ every curvature coefficient, the Ricci tensor and the Gauss-Bonnet density are confirmed to vanish. For Lemma \claimref{dark-energy.variable-exponents-residue-pointwise-corrections-are}, the displayed connection is confirmed torsion-free as an identity of the exterior algebra with the structure coefficients replaced by independent rational placeholders, and the connection with the opposite tangential sign is confirmed not to be. For Proposition \claimref{dark-energy.wall-counterterm}, the Chern-Simons form $Q$ of the Kasner connection is assembled as an exact three-form and $dQ = \epsilon_{abcd}R^{ab}\wedge R^{cd}$ confirmed identically, and the same identity is confirmed on a generic $\mathfrak{so}(1,3)$ connection with all six components nonzero and legs in all four coordinate directions, where the quartic step $\epsilon(\omega^2,\omega^2) = 0$ is exercised, and its slice component confirmed to be $8p_1p_2p_3\tau^{-2}$ at both Kasner points. For Proposition \claimref{dark-energy.cosmological-constant-does-not-change-residue}, the Bianchi I series with $\Lambda = 3$ is solved through order $\tau^5$ at the Schwarzschild exponents, the first coefficient confirmed to be $\Lambda(1-p_i)/2$, and the residuals of the evolution equations and of the constraint confirmed to vanish through order $\tau^4$, at two Kasner points and two values of $\Lambda$; the unit-boost reading of Proposition \claimref{dark-energy.frozen-point-datum-kasner-wall}(ii) is confirmed by forming $B_w^2$ on the boost plane exactly. The withdrawn radical-vanishing claim is confirmed to fail: for an explicit integer curvature-type two-form, eleven of the twelve components $E_a(\partial_3, \cdot, \cdot)$ carrying the radical leg, and three of the four cokernel components $E_3$, are nonzero.

\emph{Part C: the two kinds, and $w$.} Trace cyclicity and the derivation identity $\operatorname{tr}([X,Y]Z) + \operatorname{tr}(Y[X,Z]) = 0$ are confirmed on exact integer matrices, and $\operatorname{tr}(\alpha\wedge\beta) = \operatorname{tr}(\beta\wedge\alpha)$ for matrix-valued two-forms on an exact instance: the algebraic content of Theorem \claimref{dark-energy.gravity-pre-metric-forces-degenerate-exactly}(1). For Proposition \claimref{dark-energy.vacuum-region-registration-condition}(ii), the norm of $I_g = (1, 0, J/4)$ is confirmed to be $J/2$ as a rational-function identity in formal $J$, and the $\mu$-slot of $\nabla I_g$, formed from \claimref{dark-energy.imported-frozen-point-geometry} with a symbolic Schouten tensor, to be the trace-free Schouten tensor on an exact non-Einstein instance, and all three slots to vanish on an Einstein one; the $\rho$ slot is confirmed to be $\tfrac14\partial_aJ$ by forming $\nabla_a I_g$ from \claimref{dark-energy.imported-frozen-point-geometry} itself on a Schouten tensor whose entries are rational functions of a coordinate $s$ (the slot derivatives taken by the rational-function class, the algebraic part by \claimref{dark-energy.imported-frozen-point-geometry}), nonzero on that instance, where $J$ is not constant, and zero on an Einstein instance.

\emph{Part D: symmetry orthogonality.} On a six-mode fermionic window with exact rational occupancies, particle modes $k = 1,2,3$ and antiparticle modes $k = -1,-2,-3$, with energy $H = \sum |k| N_k$ and charge $Q_c = \sum_{k>0}N_k - \sum_{k<0}N_k$: the covariance $\langle HQ_c\rangle - \langle H\rangle\langle Q_c\rangle$ is confirmed to vanish exactly in the charge-conjugation-symmetric state and to be exactly nonzero at nonzero chemical potential. (Dictionary: the window's antiparticle mode $-k$ with occupancy $n^{\mathrm{anti}}_{k}$ is the hole at $-k$ of the singularity paper's array, $n^{\mathrm{array}}_{-k} = 1 - n^{\mathrm{anti}}_k$, so the window's criterion $n^{\mathrm{anti}}_k = n_k$ is the array criterion $n_{-k} = 1 - n_k$ of Proposition \claimref{dark-energy.acoustic-no-go-one-way-grip}.) For the charged case, the vanishing of $\langle H\,\psi^\dagger_a\psi_b\rangle$ in a diagonal state is an identity (an operator that changes the occupation has no diagonal matrix element) and is labelled so in the script; the content is the negative control, that in a pure state superposing two charge sectors the same overlap is exactly nonzero, so the $U(1)$ hypothesis of Proposition \claimref{dark-energy.acoustic-no-go-one-way-grip} is seen to be necessary on this window. The window is a free-fermion proxy for the current algebra, with $H$ as the working substitute for $L_0$; the identification with the algebra of Fact \claimref{dark-energy.imported-s-wave-current-algebra} is not tested.

\emph{Part E: the norm as a parameter of the laws.} For Proposition \claimref{dark-energy.under-action-written-norm-parameter-laws}(ii), with $M_P = 1$: $N^2 = 3/\Lambda$ is built as a rational function of a formal $\Lambda$ and its derivative confirmed to equal $-3/\Lambda^2$ and to be nonzero; the same rational function is evaluated at $\Lambda = 3$ and $\Lambda = 12$ and the two values confirmed unequal, with ratio $4 = s^2$. For the free case, at the rational instance $\Lambda = 3$ of the Goldstone checks: the three linearised constraints on the thirteen components $(\delta I, \delta V, \delta\Lambda)$ are confirmed to have rank $3$; the fifteen gauge images extended by a zero $\delta\Lambda$-component are confirmed to have rank $9$; the displayed norm mode is confirmed to satisfy all three free constraints and to violate the two fixed-$\Lambda$ constraints that involve a norm; the gauge images together with the norm mode are confirmed to have rank $10$, the whole constrained space; and the rescaling family $(sI, V/s, s^2\Lambda)$ is built as a vector of rational functions in a formal $s$, its componentwise $s$-derivative evaluated at $s = 1$ and confirmed to equal $2\Lambda$ times the norm mode, and its members confirmed to satisfy the three constraints at $s^2\Lambda$ as identities in $s$. The rank-$10$ check tests that the mode has a component outside the gauge span; that the mode and the images lie inside the constrained space is what the constraint checks confirm separately.

What the script does not check: the variational manipulations of Fact \claimref{dark-energy.imported-macdowell-mansouri-theorem-stelle-west} (imported at assembly level), the continuum limits behind Fact \claimref{dark-energy.imported-s-wave-current-algebra} and Fact \claimref{dark-energy.imported-conformal-orthogonality-sugawara-construction}, the weighted limit of Fact \claimref{dark-energy.imported-weighted-limit-schwarzschild-singularity-matching}, the assembly steps of the section ``One way to grip: the acoustic no-go'', the across-the-wall regularity statement of Theorem \claimref{dark-energy.frozen-point-makes-stelle-west-vector}(1), the half-power pole of Proposition \claimref{dark-energy.sheaf-papers-wall-soldering-variables}(i), the conformal invariance of the two-form star in Theorem \claimref{dark-energy.gravity-pre-metric-forces-degenerate-exactly}(2) and its clause (3), the boundary-term and frame statements of Proposition \claimref{dark-energy.wall-counterterm}(iii), the order counting of Lemma \claimref{dark-energy.variable-exponents-residue-pointwise-corrections-are} beyond the connection identity, the vanishing interior variation of the Gauss-Bonnet term in Theorem \claimref{dark-energy.frozen-point-makes-stelle-west-vector}(2), the charge-conjugation criterion of Proposition \claimref{dark-energy.acoustic-no-go-one-way-grip} (its window instance is the dictionary stated above), the Einstein-metric identity $-4R_{ab}R^{ab} + R^2 = 0$ behind Proposition \claimref{dark-energy.frozen-point-datum-kasner-wall}(i), the charge-zero Fock clause of Fact \claimref{dark-energy.imported-s-wave-current-algebra}, which no result here uses, and the observational registration of Proposition \claimref{dark-energy.vacuum-region-registration-condition}(iii), which is a date-stamped confrontation, not a computation.

title: Results cited, not shown
The current commutator, exactly, with its edge split
text:
In the finite window, exactly and as an operator identity,
\[
[\,a_m,\, a_m^\dagger\,] \;=\; B_m - T_m, \qquad
B_m := \sum_{k=1}^{m} N_k, \qquad T_m := \sum_{k=L-m+1}^{L} N_k ,
\]
with $N_k = \psi_k^\dagger\psi_k$: the deviation from the infinite-volume central value is a difference of \emph{edge operators}, supported on the lowest and highest $m$ modes. Consequently, for $2m \le L$, on every state in which the bottom $m$ levels are filled and the top $m$ levels are empty (an \emph{edge-clean} state), $[a_m, a_m^\dagger]$ acts as the scalar $m$: the free-boson relation holds exactly, not asymptotically, on the edge-clean subspace. Moreover $[a_m, a_{m'}] = 0$ for all $m, m'$, exactly; and for $m \neq m'$ the cross commutator $[a_m, a_{m'}^\dagger]$ is a difference of bilinears supported on the lowest and highest $\max(m, m')$ modes, which annihilates every state that is edge-clean at depth $\max(m, m')$.

text:

text:

\qquad
\tau(r) \;=\; \int_0^r A(u)^{-1/2}\,du ,
\]
where $\tau$ is proper time along the radial timelike worldlines ruling the interior, whose velocity $\hb^{-1}(x')$ is $D$-parallel (the geodesics of the derived metric), normalised so that the singularity is $\tau = 0$. In units $2M = 1$,
\[
\tau(r) \;=\; \tfrac23\, r^{3/2}\bigl(1 + \tfrac{3}{10}\,r + O(r^2)\bigr),
\qquad
r \;=\; R\,\bigl(1 - \tfrac15 R + O(R^2)\bigr), \quad R := (3\tau/2)^{2/3},
\]
and the scale factors obey $\sqrt{A} \propto \tau^{-1/3}$ and $r \propto \tau^{2/3}$ to leading order: the Kasner exponents of the approach are
\[
(p_1, p_2, p_3) \;=\; \bigl(-\tfrac13,\ \tfrac23,\ \tfrac23\bigr),
\qquad
p_1 + p_2 + p_3 \;=\; 1, \qquad p_1^2 + p_2^2 + p_3^2 \;=\; 1 .
\]

title: $\Lambda \neq 0$: the scale tractor leaves the cone
text:
Let $g$ be the derived metric of a gravitational field $(\hb, \Omega)$ on flat spacetime (Definition \claimref{obj.synthesis.gtg-flat-spacetime-gauge-fields}) and let it satisfy the Einstein condition $\Ric_{ab} = \Lambda\, g_{ab}$ on the invertible region $M^\circ$, that is $\mathcal{R}(a) = \Lambda a$ for the field strength in the conventions of the section ``Setting and conventions'', and set
\[
I_g \;:=\; \Bigl(1,\; 0,\; \tfrac{\Lambda}{6}\Bigr) \;=\; \nInf + \tfrac{\Lambda}{6}\,\nO
\]
in the scale $g$. Then $I_g$ is parallel, and every parallel section of the form $(1, 0, \rho)$ arises this way: $(1,0,\rho)$ is parallel if and only if $\rho$ is constant and $g$ is Einstein with $\Lambda = 6\rho$. The norm is
\[
Q(I_g) \;=\; \tfrac{\Lambda}{3} :
\]
the frozen point is null exactly in the $\Lambda = 0$ vacuum, and for $\Lambda \neq 0$ it leaves the cone, with the cosmological constant as its squared norm (times the positive constant $3$).
provenance: Transport Lab claim interior.scale-tractor-leaves-cone, version 7 (T06 Thm 4.7)

title: Schwarzschild-de Sitter weighted limit
text: For the Schwarzschild-de Sitter interior gravitational field $(\hb, \Omega)$ on flat spacetime (Definition \claimref{obj.synthesis.gtg-flat-spacetime-gauge-fields}), in the synchronous gauge with $A(r) = 2M/r + \Lambda r^2/3 - 1 > 0$ near $r = 0$, every function of its derived metric expressed in Kasner time acquires relative corrections of order $\Lambda r^3/M \propto \Lambda\tau^2$ against the Schwarzschild case. Consequently the Hubble-normalised connection differs from the Schwarzschild one by $O(\Lambda\tau^2)$, strictly subdominant to the $O(\tau^{2/3})$ recovery rate, and Theorem \claimref{interior.weighted-limit-theorem} holds verbatim: identical Kasner exponents $(-\tfrac13, \tfrac23, \tfrac23)$, identical boundary data, identical convergence rate. The holonomy clause is upgraded rather than weakened: for $\Lambda > 0$ the limit algebra $\mathfrak{so}(1,3)$ now lies inside the \emph{reductive} stabiliser $\mathfrak{so}(1,4)$ of the non-null parallel tractor (parallel for the $\Cl(2,4)$ tractor gauge field of Theorem \claimref{synthesis.gtg-tractor-gauge-field-reproduces-tractor-connection}) of Theorem \claimref{interior.scale-tractor-leaves-cone}, and the vanishing of the nilradical component is automatic: there is no nilradical.
provenance: Transport Lab claim interior.schwarzschild-de-sitter-weighted-limit, version 7 (T06 Thm 5.9)

title: The Schwarzschild $\varphi$-lines, exactly
text:
For the Schwarzschild interior in units $2M = 1$, along a $\varphi$-coordinate line at fixed $(r, \theta)$ the Hubble-normalised generator is constant along the line,
\begin{align*}
G \;&=\; -\bigl(\tfrac23 + \delta(r)\bigr) B_{3} + \varepsilon(r)\, R_{23}, \\
\delta(r) \;&=\; \tau\sigma_{3} - \tfrac23 \;=\; -\tfrac{2}{15}\,r - \tfrac{8}{105}\,r^{2} - \tfrac{16}{315}\,r^{3} - \cdots, \\
\varepsilon(r) \;&=\; \frac{\tau\cot\theta}{r} \;=\; \tfrac23\cot\theta\; r^{1/2}\bigl(1 + \tfrac{3}{10} r + \tfrac{9}{56} r^{2} + \cdots\bigr),
\end{align*}
so the transport over a segment of Hubble-normalised length $\lambda$ is the single exponential $\exp(\lambda G)$, the model transport is $\exp(-\tfrac23\lambda B_{3})$, and
\[
\|\exp(\lambda G) - \exp(-\tfrac23\lambda B_{3})\| \;\le\; \lambda\,(|\delta(r)| + |\varepsilon(r)|)\,e^{\lambda(1 + |\delta| + |\varepsilon|)} \;=\; O(r^{1/2}) \;=\; O(\tau^{1/3}) .
\]
The rate is $\tau^{1/3}$, slower than the $\theta$-line's $\tau^{2/3}$, and it is the sphere's intrinsic connection that sets it. Along all tangential curves of fixed Hubble-normalised length the bound of Theorem \claimref{interior.transport-level-convergence-along-tangential-curves} applies with $\|E_{\tau}\|_{K} = O(\tau^{1/3})$ away from the poles. The tangential regularity of the boundary data on the exceptional set holds by symmetry: the data are $SO(3) \times \R_{t}$-invariant, hence constant along $\mathcal{B}$ in an invariant frame and smooth in any patch.
provenance: Transport Lab claim interior.schwarzschild-lines-exactly, version 5 (T06 Cor 5.12)

title: The sign is fixed internally
text: The relative sign of the Schouten slots in \claimref{interior.imported-tractor-connection}, the $\nO \wedge \Sch(\hb^{-1}(a))$ term of the tractor gauge field of Theorem \claimref{synthesis.gtg-tractor-gauge-field-reproduces-tractor-connection}, is determined, within the conventions of the section ``Setting and conventions'', by the requirement that the flat-model section attached to a $\Lambda > 0$ Einstein representative be de Sitter space: with the signs as displayed, $\Lambda > 0$ gives $Q(I_g) = \Lambda/3 > 0$, whose flat-model section is the de Sitter pseudosphere by Proposition \claimref{interior.non-null-stabilisers-section-they-act}(2); the opposite sign choice would attach the anti-de Sitter section to $\Lambda > 0$, contradicting the naming convention $\Ric_{ab} = \Lambda g_{ab}$, $R = 4\Lambda$ for de Sitter space fixed in the section ``Setting and conventions'', which is the store's curvature sign of the field strength, $\mathcal{R}(B) = \tfrac{\Lambda}{3}B$ on de Sitter space (Definition \claimref{obj.synthesis.gtg-flat-spacetime-gauge-fields}).

title: Transport-level convergence along tangential curves, all admissible gravitational fields
text:
Let the gravitational field $(\hb, \Omega)$ on the collar be admissible (Definition \claimref{obj.interior.weighted-blow-up-hubble-normalisation-admissible}), $K \subset \mathcal{B}$ compact, and $\gamma$ a tangential curve at time $\tau$ inside $K$ of Hubble-normalised length $\lambda$, with $T_\gamma$ its $D$-transport and $T^0_\gamma$ that of the Kasner model. Then
\[
\|T_{\gamma}(\lambda) - T^{0}_{\gamma}(\lambda)\| \;\le\; \lambda\, \|E_{\tau}\|_{K}\; \exp\bigl(\lambda\,(1 + \|E_{\tau}\|_{K})\bigr),
\qquad \|E_{\tau}\|_{K} := \sup_{K}\|E_{\tau}\| ,
\]
which tends to zero as $\tau \to 0$, uniformly over all such curves of length at most $\lambda$. No control of the model transport's conjugation of the error is used.

title: The boundary mode space as matrix
text: Let the boundary mode space carry $n$ completed pairs, $n$ counted after the completion's doubling (each mode with its adjoined partner). The gauge-invariant bilinears $E_{ij} := \psi_i^\dagger \psi_j$ satisfy $[E_{ij}, E_{kl}] = \delta_{jk}E_{il} - \delta_{li}E_{kj}$ (the $\mathfrak{gl}(n)$ relations, an instance of the CAR bilinear commutator), preserve the one-particle subspace, and restrict on it to the full matrix algebra: $E_{ij}|_{\text{one-particle}} = $ the matrix unit $e_{ij}$, so the associative algebra they generate restricts onto $\Mat_n$. The doubling the completion forces is exactly what turns a tower of modes into a matrix; and matrices can be spheres.
provenance: Transport Lab claim scrambling.boundary-mode-space-matrix, version 4 (T08 Prop 5.2)

title: Consistency with the CAR construction, and the I-state's insensitivity
text: Three checks, each at its level. (i) \emph{Assembly:} the near-horizon reduction delivers one field per $(\ell, m)$ with $m$-independent dynamics, so the modular flow acts as a scalar on each multiplet and centralises the $\mathfrak{su}(2)$: the sphere's symmetry commutes with the clock. (ii) \emph{Proved:} the mixed bilinears of Proposition \claimref{scrambling.boundary-mode-space-matrix} are ordinary gauge-invariant CAR bilinears of the observable algebra: no operator outside the algebra of the boundary modes themselves is invoked. (iii) \emph{Proved, within the quasi-free setting:} the I-state with multiplet-degenerate frequencies is invariant under every gauge Bogoliubov transformation of the complexified one-particle space commuting with the one-particle Hamiltonian, in particular under all embedded $SU(2)$ actions: for a quasi-free state whose symbol is a function of the one-particle Hamiltonian, $\Lambda = g(h)$, and a unitary $U$ on the one-particle space with $UhU^* = h$, the transformed state has symbol $U\Lambda U^* = Ug(h)U^* = g(h) = \Lambda$, the same state. The I-state is embedding-insensitive: it neither selects nor obstructs the sphere. This diagonality is the sphere's side of the orthogonality no-go carried by the action paper T10 \cite{ButlerT10}: the state is insensitive to space for the same reason the gravitational sector leaves no mark on it; the full development of that identity is that paper's task (shared between the two papers).
provenance: Transport Lab claim scrambling.consistency-car-construction-i-states-insensitivity, version 5 (T08 Prop 5.6)

title: Principality from indifference: the sphere
text: Under Principle \claimref{scrambling.indifference-structural-premise-series}, the $\mathfrak{su}(2)$ structure carried by the matrix algebra of the boundary modes (Proposition \claimref{scrambling.boundary-mode-space-matrix}) is the principal embedding, uniquely: a non-principal embedding decomposes the $n$ modes into invariant blocks, a partition whose sizes and assignments nothing in the framework causes (Fact \claimref{scrambling.imported-kostant-madore-partition-data}(i)), and indifference forbids exactly such uncaused data; the principal embedding is the unique one carrying no partition data, its internal distinctions forced by the algebra once conjugation-gauge is fixed. Consequently the bilinear sector of the boundary modes is canonically Madore's fuzzy sphere, and its large-$n$ limit is the round transverse $S^2$, radius state-side: three of the four emergent dimensions now rest on the correlation structure (time and the plane from Fact \claimref{scrambling.imported-time-plane-modular-data}, the sphere from this theorem), the fourth being scale. The conclusion is conditional on Principle \claimref{scrambling.indifference-structural-premise-series} wherever this theorem is cited.

title: The degeneration sheaf
text:
Let $(M, G)$ be a tame corank-one degeneration (Hypotheses \claimref{sheaf.tameness}), $\shA = \Cl(T^*M, G)$, and write $A(x)$ for the fibre at $x$. Then:
\begin{enumerate}
\item Over $\Mo$, each fibre $A(x)$ is isomorphic to the nondegenerate Clifford algebra of the local signature; on the interior of $\Mp$ this is $\Cl(p,q)$, on the far side $\Cl(p{-}1,q{+}1)$. In the physical case these are $\Cl(1,3) \cong \Mat_2(\HH)$ and $\Cl(0,4) \cong \Mat_2(\HH)$.
\item Over $x \in \Sig$, the two-sided ideal $J(x)$ of $A(x)$ generated by the radical line $\shL(x)$ is
\[
J(x) \;=\; A(x)\,k \;=\; k\,A(x), \qquad J(x)^2 = 0, \qquad \dim_\R J(x) = 2^{n-1},
\]
for any spanning $k \in \shL(x)$, and the quotient is canonically the Clifford algebra of the induced form:
\[
A(x)/J(x) \;\cong\; \Cl\bigl(T^*_xM / \shL(x),\ \overline{G}_x\bigr),
\]
where $\overline{G}_x$ is nondegenerate of rank $n-1$ and signature $(p{-}1, q)$.
\item The fibrewise ideals assemble: the multiplication map $\shA|_\Sig \otimes \shL \to \shA|_\Sig$ has image a smooth subbundle $\shA|_\Sig \cdot \shL$ of rank $2^{n-1}$, and its pushforward
\[
\shJ \;:=\; i_*\bigl(\shA|_\Sig \cdot \shL\bigr) \qquad (i : \Sig \hookrightarrow M)
\]
is a finitely presented sheaf of $\mathcal{O}_M$-modules and of $\shA$-bimodules, supported exactly on $\Sig$, with fibre $J(x)$ at $x \in \Sig$ and fibre $0$ elsewhere. The associated ideal sheaf of $\shA$ is the kernel
\[
\shK \;:=\; \ker\bigl(\shA \longrightarrow i_*\bigl(\shA|_\Sig \,/\, \shA|_\Sig \cdot \shL\bigr)\bigr),
\]
a sheaf of two-sided ideals of $\shA$ whose restriction to $\Sig$ realises $J(x)$ fibrewise and whose quotient $\shA/\shK$ is the pushforward of the quotient bundle of (2).
\end{enumerate}
provenance: Transport Lab claim sheaf.degeneration-sheaf, version 5 (T04 Thm 3.1)

title: Localised transport
text: The subalgebra of $\shC$ generated by $T^*M$ is canonically isomorphic to $\shA$, globally, including over $\Sig$, because $h$ restricted to $T^*M$ equals $G$ identically by construction. Over $\Mo \cap \Mp$ the inclusion $\shA \subset \shC$ is fibrewise the conformal embedding $\Cl(p,q) \subset \Cl(p{+}1,q{+}1)$ of Rule 1 \cite{ButlerT1}. Over $\Sig$ the very same elements change ideal-theoretic character: a radical covector $k$ satisfies $k^2 = 0$ in both algebras, but the two-sided ideal it generates is square-zero in $A(x)$ (Theorem \claimref{sheaf.degeneration-sheaf}) and is the whole algebra in $C(x)$ (Proposition \claimref{sheaf.resolution-ideal-theoretically}), where $k$ acquires a partner $k^*$ built from the coupling, with $kk^* + k^*k = 1$ and $(k^*)^2 = 0$. The completion does not modify the degenerate algebra; it re-embeds it where its infinitesimals cease to be infinitesimal. In particular the localised ladder pair $(k, k^*)$ exists exactly over $\Sig$: the CAR structure of the series' operator-algebraic reading is supported on the singular locus.
provenance: Transport Lab claim sheaf.localised-transport, version 5 (T04 Cor 4.5)

title: The matching at connection level
text:
For the Schwarzschild interior gravitational field $(\hb, \Omega)$ on flat spacetime (Definition \claimref{obj.synthesis.gtg-flat-spacetime-gauge-fields}), write $(d\tau, \theta^1, \theta^2, \theta^3)$ for the adapted orthonormal coframe of Fact \claimref{obj.interior.weighted-blow-up-hubble-normalisation-admissible} (synchronous time, normalised Killing direction, sphere directions): the components $\theta^a(v) = \gamma^a \cdot \hb^{-1}(v)$ of the physical-vector map in the adapted orthonormal frame. Then:
\begin{enumerate}
\item \emph{(Frames.)} The adapted coframe consists of exceptional-module sections, exactly: $\sqrt{m^2 - r}\;d\tau = \rho$ and
\[
\sqrt{m^2 - r}\;\theta^1 \;=\; -\sqrt r\,\dtPG \,+\, m\,(k/\sqrt r),
\]
with $\theta^2 = \mu_1$, $\theta^3 = \mu_2$ exactly (the first identity uses the transition of Theorem \claimref{sheaf.schwarzschild-degeneration-boundary-tame}(4)). The static and rain frames of $\shW_{\mathrm{exc}}$ are related by the rotation-gauge boost of rapidity $\chi$ with $(\sinh\chi, \cosh\chi) = (-\sqrt r, m)/\sqrt{m^2-r}$, unit-normalised exactly and vanishing on the exceptional boundary: the two frames coincide at the wall, future orientations matched.
\item \emph{(Rates.)} In this common frame the Hubble-normalised rotation-gauge field is $-\sum_i (\tau\sigma_i)B_i \otimes \hat\theta^i$ (in the sign of the Definition) plus a sphere term of normalised size $\tau/r = \tfrac23\sqrt r + O(r^{3/2}) \to 0$, with the exact series of Fact \claimref{obj.interior.weighted-blow-up-hubble-normalisation-admissible} re-derived here independently by exact power series in $\sqrt r$, agreeing coefficient by coefficient, and the trace rule $\tau(\sigma_1 + 2\sigma_2) \to 1$ realising the first Kasner relation as a rate statement.
\item \emph{(The matching.)} Consequently the weighted-limit connection of Fact \claimref{obj.interior.weighted-blow-up-hubble-normalisation-admissible} is a connection datum on the exceptional bundle of this section: its boundary value is minus the weight one-form of the exceptional coframe, $-\sum_i p_i B_i \otimes \hat\nu^i$, its total element is $-B_w$, minus the unit boost $B_w$ of Proposition \claimref{sheaf.matching-fibre}, and its values, nonzero multiples of the three boosts, generate the full bivector algebra, so the holonomy theorem of \cite{ButlerT6} is the statement that the boundary holonomy of the exceptional bundle, in the values-level sense of \cite[Def.~5.5]{ButlerT6}, is all of $\mathfrak{so}(1,3)$; the matching uses exactly those values. The two black-hole routes are one structure: the weighted limit transports the exceptional fibre, the completion Clifford-multiplies it, and the ladder boost is the transverse $\mathfrak{so}(1,1)$.
\end{enumerate}
provenance: Transport Lab claim sheaf.matching-connection-level, version 7 (T04 Thm 8.27)

title: The matching at the fibre
text: Normalise the exceptional Gram to $\eta = \operatorname{diag}(1,-1,-1,-1)$, with $\hat e_0$ the proper-time direction and $\hat e_i$ the Kasner eigendirections. Then: (1) the bivector algebra of the exceptional fibre is $\mathfrak{so}(1,3)$, the holonomy algebra of Fact \claimref{obj.interior.weighted-blow-up-hubble-normalisation-admissible}, and the identification of the two fibres matching proper time, eigendirections, and exponents is canonical up to the isometries preserving the Kasner data; (2) under it, the surviving value $-\sum_i p_i B_i$ of the Hubble-normalised rotation-gauge field (in the sign of the Gauge Theory Gravity definition, $D_a = a \cdot \nabla + \Omega(a) \times$) corresponds to $-B_w$, minus the \emph{weight bivector} $B_w = \sum_i p_i\,\hat e_0 \wedge \hat e_i$, because the weights of the sheaf construction are forced to equal the exponents (Theorem \claimref{sheaf.weights-are-forced-are-kasner-exponents}); (3) $B_w$ is $\eta$-antisymmetric with characteristic polynomial $\lambda^4 - (\sum_i p_i^2)\lambda^2 = \lambda^4 - \lambda^2$: \emph{the second Kasner relation says precisely that the surviving matrix is a unit boost of the exceptional algebra}. The wall itself carries the transverse generator: the ladder boost $K = \tfrac12[k,k^*] = k \wedge k^* = N - \tfrac12$ (no relation to the exterior form $K$ of Theorem \claimref{sheaf.conservation-degeneracy-absolute-form}), with $K^2 = \tfrac14$ on the whole ambient fibre, an $\mathfrak{so}(1,1)$ supported on the wall.
provenance: Transport Lab claim sheaf.matching-fibre, version 4 (T04 Prop 8.26)

title: The metric's residue, and the square-root twist
text:
At a tame wall the physical metric (the inverse cometric) has a canonical simple pole: for any defining function $\tau$ of $\Sig$,
\[
O \;:=\; \lim_{\tau \to 0}\, \tau\, G^{-1} \;=\; \frac{k \otimes k}{\delta(k \otimes k)/d\tau} ,
\]
a nowhere-vanishing section of $\shL \otimes \shL$ depending on $\tau$ through the weight of a section of $\shL \otimes \shL \otimes N\Sig$; invariantly, the residue is $\delta^{-1}$, the inverse of the transversality datum of Lemma \claimref{sheaf.invariant-form-t3}, regarded as a section of $\shL \otimes \shL \otimes N\Sig = \operatorname{Hom}(N^*\Sig, \shL^{\otimes 2})$. It is a nondegenerate pairing between $\shL^* \otimes \shL^*$ and $N^*\Sig$, hence induces a canonical isomorphism
\[
N^*\Sig \;\cong\; \shL^{\otimes 2} :
\]
the conormal bundle is the square of the dying direction itself. Dually, $N\Sig \cong (\shL^*)^{\otimes 2}$: the Witt partner line adjoined by the completion, which the pairing normalisation $kk^* + k^*k = 1$ identifies with $\shL^*$, is a canonical square root of the \emph{normal} bundle, and the dying line $\shL$ is a canonical square root of the conormal bundle. (The reading of the blow-up rescaling $k \mapsto k/\sqrt{t}$ as the normalisation of a conormal square root is Remark \claimref{note.sheaf.blow-up-dictionary}.)

title: The bosonisation bridge, s-wave sector
text:
Let $\{\psi_k, \psi^\dagger_k\}_{k \in \mathbb{Z}}$ be the boundary modes, as fermion operators on the filled-sea Fock space (the infinite filled-sea array whose algebraic model is the completed tower limit of \cite[Thm.~5.6]{ButlerT3}, cited for the structure; its provenance here is the s-wave aggregation declared above, not a tower, the mod-8 clock having stopped after one ascent), and define the currents $a_m := \sum_k :\psi^\dagger_k\,\psi_{k+m}:$ with $:\;:$ normal ordering at the sea level; with the sea filled below the level, $a_m$ annihilates the sea for $m > 0$ and $a_{-m} = a_m^{\dagger}$ creates particle-hole pairs. (The opposite index convention flips the sign of the central term; the verification script fixes the convention by computation.) Then:
\begin{enumerate}
\item (Current algebra.) $[a_m, a_n] = m\,\delta_{m+n,0}\,\id$ on the infinite array; on a finite window the commutator equals $m\,\delta_{m+n,0}\,\id$ plus an \emph{exactly identified} edge operator ($B_m - T_m - m$ in the proof's notation), supported on the bottom and top $m$ sites and vanishing on all bulk states: the number-conserving bilinears satisfy the canonical commutation relations of a free boson. A boson is a pair of the pair.
\item (KMS restriction.) Each bilinear $\psi^\dagger_k\psi_{k+m}$ carries a definite boost weight, fixed by the difference $\omega_{k+m} - \omega_k$ of its two modes' weights. Under (Q)'s weight clause, $\omega_k = \kappa k$, that difference is $\kappa m$ for every $k$, so each current $a_m$ is itself a weight vector and the current subalgebra is globally invariant under the modular flow of Theorem \claimref{singularity.modular-structure-completed-pair}; for weights that are not affine in $k$ the summands of $a_m$ rotate at different rates and the span of the currents need not be invariant, so this invariance uses (Q). Under (Q) the joint state is KMS for that flow, and a KMS state restricted to a flow-invariant subalgebra is KMS at the same temperature for the restricted flow. Without (Q) no joint KMS state is available: (R) is imposed on the marginals alone, and Theorem \claimref{singularity.exact-equilibrium-over-determines-boundary-modes} is the reason its joint form is rejected elsewhere in the chain.
\item (The Planck factor.) Under (Q), with the marginal occupancies $n_k = (e^{\beta\omega_k} + 1)^{-1} = (e^{\beta\kappa k} + 1)^{-1}$ at the premise's linear weights, the current occupancy is, exactly,
\[
\langle a_{-m} a_m \rangle \;=\; \sum_{k \in \mathbb{Z}} n_{k+m}\,(1 - n_k) \;=\; \frac{m}{e^{\beta\kappa m} - 1} \qquad (m > 0) ,
\]
with no vacuum piece in this convention ($a_m$ annihilates the sea): Bose-Einstein occupancy at exactly $\TH$. The Planck spectrum of the bosonic Hawking flux is derived, not conjectured, for the s-wave sector, in the equilibrium reading (Q) fixes; for a general member of the chain's state class the left side acquires the connected correlators (Q) sets to zero, and no exact spectrum is claimed.
\end{enumerate}
The single assembly-level ingredient in the section is the charge-zero Fock isomorphism (the charge-zero sector of the fermionic Fock space is canonically the bosonic Fock space, with fermions recovered as vertex operators), cited to \cite{PressleySegal1986} and used only for the completeness statement that the two descriptions are one algebra; parts (1)-(3) are proved outright.

title: The trichotomy: what kind of number $N$ is
text:
The question the paper ends by pointing at can itself be classified. The classification has four parts, of which the first contains a proved statement and a reading, the second is an import, the third is conditional on the first two, on Observation \claimref{standard-model.dating-descent} and on a decision the fourth names, and the fourth is imported from the action paper; the levels are marked clause by clause.
\begin{enumerate}
\item \emph{(Kinematic.)} Proved: under $\Lambda \to s^{2}\Lambda$ at fixed $M_{P}$, that is $I \to sI$ on the frozen point with the conformal class unchanged, $H \to sH$ and $N \to N/s$, while every discrete invariant this paper derives (the algebra and its dimension twelve, the global form and its $\mathbb{Z}_{6}$, the dimension four, the content and the hypercharges, and under (S) the ratio $3/8$) is unchanged, since each is computed from the conformal class, the pair structure and the group alone, none of which the rescaling affects. Reading, at observation level: since the conformal class and the pair structure carry no scale, no construction from them alone can fix $N$, which lies in the ratio of the frozen point's norm to the Planck scale; on this reading the kinematic layer determines all discrete invariants and no continuous modulus, and $N$ and the weight spectrum are its only continuous moduli.
\item \emph{(Non-dynamical, imported.)} $\Lambda$ is the norm of the frozen point, and the norm is not a field: it is fixed by a constraint, the fluctuations of the frozen point are pure gauge, and the action carries no equation of motion for it (Fact \claimref{standard-model.imported-norm-frozen-point-not-field}).
\item \emph{(Initial data, conditional.)} If the alternatives kinematic, dynamical and initial-data are exhaustive, then by (1) and (2) $N$ is initial data, and Observation \claimref{standard-model.dating-descent}(ii) locates the boundary that carries it at the origin. The exhaustiveness is not proved here, and the location is an Observation; the clause is conditional on both, and clause (4) says what the exhaustiveness costs.
\item \emph{(Parameter of the laws, imported.)} The three alternatives are not exhaustive: a conserved quantity that is constant on every solution of a theory but varies across a family of theories indexed by a parameter is a parameter of the laws, and the action paper proves that under the action as written, with $\Lambda$ the value of the Stelle-West constraints fixed before variation, $N$ is exactly that: constant on each solution space $\mathcal{S}_{\Lambda}$ by the rigidity of (2), varying across $\Lambda$, so neither dynamically fixed nor initial data \cite[Prop.~5.8]{ButlerT10}. Clause (3) therefore holds only if the norm is promoted from a fixed number to the value of a Lagrange-multiplier field whose constancy is an equation of motion, the Henneaux-Teitelboim mechanism, which makes $\Lambda$ a label of the solution rather than of the theory; that promotion is a decision for the series, recorded open with both branches stated \cite[Rem.~5.9]{ButlerT10}, and the entropic and null-endpoint effects named below act on a measure over theories or on a measure within one theory according to it.
\end{enumerate}
